CVE-2026-19478.body:
# CVE-2026-19478 — GitLab Critical GraphQL Flaw: Unauthenticated Modification/Deletion of Public Projects (CVSS 9.4)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Type:** CVE / unauthenticated authorization bypass (GraphQL) | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 9.4) | **Date:** 2026-08-17

## Summary
GitLab released an **out-of-band critical patch on 17 August 2026** for **CVE-2026-19478**, affecting **Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE)**. Under certain conditions an **unauthenticated attacker can remotely modify or delete public projects and user data**.

## Root Cause (verified)
**Code injection via a GraphQL directive.** Under certain conditions this permits a remote, unauthenticated user to alter or delete public projects and user data.

## Companion Vulnerability — CVE-2026-19650 (CVSS 7.1, High)
The same patch release also fixes **CVE-2026-19650**, a **cross-site request forgery flaw in the GraphQL multiplex query handler**. Improper request validation allows **unauthenticated users to execute mutations through GET requests**.

That second bug is worth attention in its own right: **state-changing GraphQL mutations reachable via GET** breaks the safe-method assumption that CSRF defences, caching layers, proxies, and browser prefetching all rely on. A GET-reachable mutation can be triggered by an image tag, a link prefetch, or a logging proxy replaying a URL.

## Why the Release Timing Is a Signal
GitLab patches on a fixed schedule — **twice monthly, second and fourth Wednesdays**. This release came **off-schedule, five days after a routine patch that contained no critical issues**. An out-of-band critical release is GitLab telling you, implicitly, that this could not wait two weeks. Treat accordingly.

## Affected / Fixed
**Affected versions:**
- All versions from **18.2** before **18.11.11**
- **19.0** before 19.0.8
- **19.1** before 19.1.6
- **19.2** before 19.2.4

**Fixed in:** **19.2.4, 19.1.6, 19.0.8, 18.11.11**

**Only self-managed installations need to act.** GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated already run patched versions — no customer action required there.

## Impact Assessment
This is a **destructive-integrity** bug rather than a data-theft bug: unauthenticated *modification or deletion*. For a source-control platform that maps to:
- Loss of public repositories and their history
- Tampering with public project contents (a **supply-chain vector** if downstream consumers pull from those projects)
- User data modification/deletion

The tampering angle deserves attention — silent modification of a public project is more dangerous than deletion, because deletion is noticed immediately and modification may not be.

## Action
- **Self-managed GitLab: patch now** to 19.2.4 / 19.1.6 / 19.0.8 / 18.11.11.
- Until patched, restrict network access to the GitLab instance.
- After patching, verify integrity of public projects: compare repository refs/commit hashes against known-good mirrors or developer clones.
- Confirm backups are current and restorable before assuming deletion is recoverable.
- Review GraphQL endpoint access logs for unauthenticated mutation attempts — **including GET requests carrying mutations** (CVE-2026-19650).

## Bug Bounty / Research Relevance
Two GraphQL bugs in one release, both unauthenticated, is a useful signal about where GitLab's attack surface currently sits. Productive hunting patterns visible here:
- **GraphQL directives as an injection sink** — directives are processed before/around normal resolver authorization and are routinely under-tested.
- **Multiplex/batch query handlers** — batching endpoints often bypass the per-request middleware (CSRF, method checks, rate limits) applied to single queries.
- **HTTP-method confusion on mutations** — if a GraphQL endpoint accepts GET, test whether mutations execute.

> Sources: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-gitlab-graphql-flaw-could-let.html) — 17 Aug 2026 · [GitLab patch release notes](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-2-4-released/) (primary) · [Cyberpress](https://cyberpress.org/gitlab-critical-vulnerability/) · [GBHackers](https://gbhackers.com/gitlab-patches-multiple-security-flaws/)


## Tags
 #cve #CVE-2026-19478 #CVE-2026-19650 #gitlab #graphql #code-injection #csrf #authorization-bypass #unauthenticated #self-managed #supply-chain #bug-bounty #critical #unverified


---

## Update — 2026-08-21: Active Exploitation Confirmed

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/) "GitLab CVE-2026-19478 Comes Under Active Exploitation Within Days of Disclosure" — 2026-08-21 | X: @TheHackersNews `2090697703953203315` (2026-08-21)

**CVE-2026-19478 is now being actively exploited**, with unauthenticated attackers modifying or deleting public projects. Exploitation began **within days of the 17 August out-of-band disclosure**.

**This closes the loop on the original note's assessment.** The out-of-band release timing was read here as GitLab signalling that the flaw could not wait for the normal cycle; four days later that read is confirmed by exploitation in the wild.

### Revised urgency
- Self-managed GitLab still on ≤19.2.3 / 19.1.5 / 19.0.7 / 18.11.10 should be treated as **presumed-compromised**, not merely unpatched.
- **Integrity verification is no longer optional.** Compare repository refs and commit hashes against developer clones or mirrors. Silent modification of a public project is the higher-consequence outcome (supply-chain vector) and will not announce itself the way deletion does.
- Preserve GraphQL endpoint logs before rotation — including **GET requests carrying mutations** (companion CVE-2026-19650).

**Type:** CVE / authentication bypass + memory overflow | **Severity:** Critical (CVE-2026-19490, CVSS 9.3) + High (CVE-2026-19489, CVSS 8.8) | **Date:** 2026-08-20

## Summary
Citrix patched two flaws in **NetScaler ADC** and **NetScaler Gateway**:

| CVE | CVSS | Class |
|---|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-19490** | **9.3** | **Authentication bypass** — no credentials, no user interaction, on certain Gateway and AAA server configurations |
| CVE-2026-19489 | 8.8 | Memory overflow |

## Affected Versions
- NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway **14.1 before 14.1-73.32**
- NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway **13.1 before 13.1-63.21**
- NetScaler ADC **FIPS before 14.1-73.32 FIPS**
- NetScaler ADC **FIPS and NDcPP before 13.1-37.277**

Also affects **SecurAccess ZTNA Hybrid** deployments that use customer-managed NetScaler instances.

**Not affected:** Citrix-managed cloud services and Citrix-managed Adaptive Authentication — already patched by Citrix.

## Why This Is Urgent
NetScaler Gateway is an **internet-facing remote-access chokepoint**. The historical pattern for this product line (CitrixBleed and its successors) is short: bulletin → mass scanning → exploitation, often within days. An **unauthenticated, no-interaction auth bypass on the AAA/Gateway path** is the highest-value class of bug an edge appliance can have — it converts directly into session/identity access rather than just code on a box.

Note also that patching alone has historically been insufficient for this product family: session tokens minted before patching can survive the update.

## Action
1. **Patch immediately** to 14.1-73.32 / 13.1-63.21 / 14.1-73.32 FIPS / 13.1-37.277.
2. After patching, **terminate all active ICA and PCoIP sessions** and invalidate existing sessions — do not assume the update revokes pre-existing tokens.
3. Review authentication logs for successful logins without corresponding credential events, especially against AAA virtual servers.
4. Confirm whether any **SecurAccess ZTNA Hybrid** deployment points at a customer-managed NetScaler — those inherit the exposure.
5. Rotate credentials for accounts that authenticate through the Gateway if compromise cannot be excluded.

# CVE-2026-19598 — WordPress Pods Plugin — Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation (CVSS 9.8, WordPress.org force-update)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

> Source: [@IntCyberDigest](https://x.com/IntCyberDigest/status/2091982627930779913) — Mon, 24 Aug 2026 20:15 UTC
> Corroboration: Patchstack; Wordfence (100,000 sites); gbhackers; published 15 Aug 2026

## Summary
The `pods_admin` AJAX router treats **any** request through the JSON meta-box-loader path as a failure via `pods_error()` — and in doing so **skips all access checks, capability gates, nonce verification and login enforcement**. An unauthenticated attacker can invoke administrative methods directly, including **overwriting any user's password** — site owner included — for full takeover.

Affects **all versions up to and including 3.3.9**. Over **100,000 active installations**.

## The notable part
WordPress.org is running a **force-update** across vulnerable installs. That is reserved for flaws judged too dangerous to leave to admin discretion — a useful severity signal independent of the CVSS number.

## Fixed in
**3.3.9.1**, with backports to **3.2.8.3, 3.1.4.2, 3.0.10.4, 2.9.19.4, 2.8.23.4**.

## Actions
- Verify the force-update actually landed — sites with auto-update disabled will not receive it.
- Review administrator accounts for unauthorized additions or role changes.
- Reset privileged passwords where compromise is plausible.
- Grep access logs for POSTs to the Pods AJAX endpoint, particularly the meta-box-loader path.

## Pattern note
Second WordPress auth/authz bypass in this sweep alongside [[CVE-2026-61979-15981-miniOrange-SAML-SSO-WordPress-Auth-Bypass-Exploited]]. Both are **authorization logic that fails open** — an error path that returns without enforcing, rather than a memory-safety or injection bug.

---

## Update 2026-08-30 — third-party confirmation, and context

Confirmed again by The Hacker News reporting Wordfence/Patchstack, at **CVSS 9.8**, affecting **all versions up to and including 3.3.9** — consistent with everything recorded above. No new technical detail; recording it because it is the second independent confirmation of the same figures.

Pods now sits inside a five-flaw WordPress cluster disclosed the same day. See [[WordPress-Five-Critical-Plugin-Theme-Flaws-2026-08-29]] for the roundup and the shared pattern — **three of the five are authorization logic that fails open**, which is exactly the Pods failure mode identified in this note (an error path that returns before enforcing capability, nonce and login checks).

# CVE-2026-21962 — Oracle HTTP Server / WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in — Unauthenticated Critical-Data Access (CVSS 10.0, KEV)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/actively-exploited-oracle-weblogic-flaw.html) — Tue, 25 Aug 2026 06:12 UTC
> Corroboration: CISA KEV addition 2026-08-24; CCCS AV26-042 Update 2 (2026-08-24); NetSPI; eSecurity Planet; GreyNoise / CloudSEK telemetry

## Summary
Improper access control in the Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in lets an **unauthenticated** attacker with network access over **HTTP** obtain unauthorized **create, delete or modify** access to critical data. CVSS **10.0**. Now **actively exploited** and added to the CISA KEV catalog.

## Affected
- Oracle HTTP Server and proxy plug-ins **12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0, 14.1.2.0.0**
- WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in **for IIS** on **12.2.1.4.0**

## Timeline — the important part
- **January 2026** — Oracle ships the fix in the January quarterly CPU.
- **22 Jan 2026** — public exploit code appears.
- **Immediately after** — CloudSEK's high-interaction honeypot records automated exploitation attempts.
- **24 Aug 2026** — CISA adds to KEV; CCCS reissues the January Oracle advisory as **Update 2**.

**Read:** this is not a new vulnerability — it is a **seven-month-old patched flaw being re-escalated** because exploitation finally reached a volume CISA acts on. The exposure is unpatched edge proxy tiers, not a zero-day.

## Impact
Unauthorized access to internal WebLogic endpoints, potential remote code execution, full backend compromise, and lateral movement from the proxy tier inward. The plug-in sits at the **edge**, in front of the app server — a compromised proxy is a trusted position.

## Actions
- Confirm the January 2026 CPU is applied to **OHS and the proxy plug-in specifically** — patching WebLogic core does not patch the plug-in.
- Inventory IIS-hosted proxy plug-in instances (12.2.1.4.0) — commonly missed in Oracle patch cycles.
- Hunt inbound HTTP against proxy endpoints since **late January 2026**, not just recent days.

CVE-2026-32475.body:
# CVE-2026-32475 — Elementor Pro (WordPress): Empty-Filename Parser Confusion → Unauthenticated File Upload RCE

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-elementor-pro-bug-exposes-wordpress-sites-to-rce-attacks/) — 2026-08-20 | [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/) 2026-08-20 | Primary research: **Patchstack**


**Type:** CVE / arbitrary file upload → RCE | **Severity:** Critical | **Date:** 2026-08-20

## Summary
**CVE-2026-32475** affects **Elementor Pro before 4.2.2**. The **File Upload module** uses **separate loops for validation and for processing**, and the two loops **disagree about how to handle an empty file entry** (an upload part whose filename is blank, which PHP reports as `UPLOAD_ERR_NO_FILE`).

Per Patchstack: *"The validation loop and the processing loop have different early-exit logic for these empty entries, so a carefully shaped multi-part upload can be seen one way by the validator and another way by the mover."*

## Exploitation Shape
Craft a multipart upload where **the first entry has an empty filename**, followed by a **malicious entry**. The validator's early-exit skips or mis-indexes; the processing loop moves the attacker's file. Result: **executable file written to the server → RCE**.

## The Pattern Worth Internalising
This is a **parser-differential / TOCTOU-by-iteration** bug, not a blocklist bypass. Two passes over the same input with different loop-termination semantics is a recurring root cause across languages and frameworks. It generalises well as a **hunting heuristic**:

> Wherever code validates a collection in one loop and acts on it in another, look for an input that changes the iteration boundary between the two.

Compare **CVE-2026-15748 (Forminator)** from three days earlier — also an unauthenticated WordPress upload-to-RCE, but a blocklist/MIME-key bypass rather than a loop mismatch. See `CVE-2026-15748-Forminator-WordPress-Unauth-FileUpload-RCE.md`.

## Action
- **Update Elementor Pro to 4.2.2 or later** immediately. Elementor Pro is on millions of sites; expect mass scanning.
- Audit `wp-content/uploads/` (and any custom upload path) for **`.php`, `.phtml`, `.phar`** and other executable extensions with recent mtimes.
- Enforce **no PHP execution in the uploads directory** at the web-server level — this defence would have neutralised both this bug and Forminator.
- Review web-server access logs for POST requests to Elementor form endpoints with multipart bodies containing empty filename parts.

#cve #wordpress #elementor #file-upload #rce #parser-differential #unauthenticated #critical

## Tags
 #unverified

---

## Update — 2026-09-04: Confirmed mass exploitation — Wordfence blocked 440,000+ attempts; Super Forms exploited alongside

**Status change: this is now actively exploited at scale.** Wordfence reports blocking **over 440,000 exploitation attempts** against **CVE-2026-32475 (Elementor Pro)** and a parallel flaw in **Super Forms**. Attacks deliver a **webshell** and execute arbitrary commands on the underlying server.

**Both bugs allow unauthenticated PHP uploads.** The Elementor Pro attacks carry a specific precondition worth recording, because it defines who is actually at risk: **exploitation requires a published page containing a Form widget with a File Upload field.** An installed-but-unused Elementor Pro is not exploitable by this path; a site with a live contact or application form that accepts attachments is.

### What the precondition changes about triage

This turns a blanket "millions of sites affected" into a **checkable question with a yes/no answer**: *do we have a published page with an Elementor form that accepts file uploads?* That is a five-minute audit and it correctly separates the urgent population from the merely unpatched one.

It also identifies **which** sites are exposed, and they are the worst ones — public contact forms, job-application pages, support-request forms. These are pages that exist to receive files from strangers, are linked from the site's own navigation, and are therefore trivially discoverable by the same crawl that finds them for legitimate visitors. **The attacker's targeting problem is solved by the victim's site map.**

### Action (updated — treat as compromise-assessment, not patching)

1. **Patch is necessary but no longer sufficient.** At 440,000 blocked attempts, the relevant question for any site that was unpatched and had a qualifying form published is **whether it was already hit**, not whether it will be.
2. **Audit for the precondition first** — list published pages with Elementor Form widgets containing File Upload fields. That is your exposed set.
3. **Hunt for webshells** across `wp-content/uploads/` and any custom upload path: `.php`, `.phtml`, `.phar`, and PHP content in files with image extensions. Check mtimes against the disclosure date, and check for files whose extension does not match their magic bytes.
4. **Check for the second bug too** — **Super Forms** is exploited in the same campaign by the same unauthenticated-PHP-upload path. Patch and audit both.
5. **Enforce no PHP execution in upload directories at the web-server level.** This is now the third WordPress upload-RCE in this vault (Elementor Pro, Super Forms, Forminator) that this one control would have neutralised outright, independent of patch state.
6. Rotate WordPress salts, admin credentials, and any database or API credentials in `wp-config.php` on sites assessed as compromised.

### Cross-reference

Logged the same day as the CVE assignment for **CVE-2026-19949 (All-in-One WP Migration and Backup, 3M+ sites)** — see that note. **Two mass-deployed WordPress plugin flaws in one window, one confirmed under exploitation at scale, indicates an active ecosystem-wide campaign** rather than isolated disclosures.

> Source: [@TheHackersNews](https://x.com/TheHackersNews/status/2095796361019244588) — 2026-09-04 08:49 UTC — "Attackers are exploiting Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE flaws. Wordfence has blocked over 440,000 attempts. Both bugs allow unauthenticated PHP uploads; Elementor attacks require a published page with a Form widget and File Upload field."

# CVE-2026-34197 — Apache ActiveMQ Classic RCE via Jolokia API

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Date**: 2026-04-08
**Tags**: #cve #rce #apache #activemq #jolokia #jmx #critical #ai-discovered #horizon3
**Source**: X (@Horizon3Attack) — [https://x.com/Horizon3Attack/status/2041614428752286134](https://x.com/Horizon3Attack/status/2041614428752286134)
**CVE**: CVE-2026-34197
**Severity**: Critical
**Component**: Apache ActiveMQ Classic — web console (Jolokia API endpoint)
**Discovered by**: Horizon3 Attack Team using **Claude AI**

---

## Summary

A **remote code execution vulnerability** in the Apache ActiveMQ Classic web console, exploitable via the **Jolokia API**. The vulnerability is:
- Exploitable with **default credentials** on unmodified deployments
- Exploitable **completely unauthenticated** on certain configurations
- Discovered through AI-assisted vulnerability research using **Claude**

---

## Technical Details

### Attack Vector
The Jolokia API (`/api/jolokia`) provides a JMX-over-HTTP interface to the ActiveMQ broker. This endpoint, when accessible:
1. Allows invocation of arbitrary MBean operations via JSON HTTP requests
2. With default/weak credentials (admin:admin), attacker can invoke `exec` MBean methods
3. Certain non-default configurations expose Jolokia without authentication entirely

### Exploitation
- Target: ActiveMQ Classic web console, typically on port 8161
- Endpoint: `/api/jolokia` or `/jolokia`
- Method: POST request invoking ClassLoader or thread class loading MBean to load remote code
- Impact: Full RCE as the ActiveMQ service account

---

## Affected Configurations

- ActiveMQ Classic with Jolokia enabled (default in many versions)
- Default credentials not changed (admin:admin)
- OR Jolokia endpoint exposed without authentication

---

## Exploitation Indicators

- POST requests to `/api/jolokia` or `/jolokia` with `exec` or `read` operations
- Class loading from external URLs in ActiveMQ logs
- Unusual outbound connections from ActiveMQ service process
- ActiveMQ spawning child processes (shell, java -jar, curl, wget)

---

## Remediation

1. Apply Apache ActiveMQ patch for CVE-2026-34197 immediately
2. **Change default credentials** (admin:admin) if not already done
3. Restrict access to the web console and Jolokia endpoint (firewall, VPN)
4. If Jolokia is not needed, **disable it** in `activemq.xml`
5. Monitor ActiveMQ for unusual JMX/MBean invocations

---

## AI Discovery Note

> This CVE was discovered by Horizon3's Attack Team **using Claude AI** to analyze the ActiveMQ Classic codebase and API surface. This is another data point that AI-assisted vuln research is producing real, critical findings.

See also: [[ai-bugbounty-autonomous-hacking-guide]], [[ai-bugbounty-claude-zeroday-ghost-cms]]

# CVE-2026-40008 — Apache IoTDB Pipe Processor Unauthenticated Deserialization RCE

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** Critical — CVSS 9.8 (no authentication)
**Component:** Apache IoTDB — pipe processor (RPC interface)
**Impact:** Unauthenticated remote code execution via insecure Java object instantiation.

## Details
The Apache IoTDB pipe processor accepts a **fully-qualified Java class name over RPC and instantiates it** with no authentication and no allow-list. An attacker with network access to the RPC interface can trigger arbitrary class instantiation at the network level — a classic unsafe-deserialization / arbitrary-class-load primitive that leads to remote code execution.

## Action
- Patch to the fixed Apache IoTDB release once published; monitor the Apache advisory / NVD entry for exact fixed version.
- Restrict the IoTDB RPC interface to trusted networks; never expose it to the internet.
- Add network ACLs / firewalling in front of the RPC port as an interim control.

CVE-2026-42530.body:
# CVE-2026-42530 & CVE-2026-42055 — Critical NGINX Open Source RCE (F5 OOB Patch)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 7 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical — CVSSv4 **9.2** (both)
**Product:** NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus
**Type:** Use-after-free (HTTP/3 QUIC) and heap-based buffer overflow (HTTP/2 proxy)
**Status:** Patched out-of-band by F5; unauthenticated, remote

## Summary
F5 issued **out-of-band patches** for two critical NGINX flaws, both remotely triggerable by an **unauthenticated** attacker and capable of leading to **remote code execution**.

### CVE-2026-42530 (CVSSv4 9.2) — HTTP/3 QUIC use-after-free
Use-after-free in **`ngx_http_v3_module`**, triggered when NGINX is configured with the **HTTP/3 QUIC module**. A specially crafted HTTP/3 session can **reopen a QPACK encoder stream**, causing a use-after-free in the NGINX worker process (worker restart/DoS). If **ASLR is disabled or bypassed**, the attacker can execute arbitrary code.
- Affects NGINX Open Source **1.31.0 / 1.31.1**; fixed in **1.31.2**.
- Mitigation: **disable HTTP/3**.

### CVE-2026-42055 (CVSSv4 9.2) — HTTP/2 proxy heap overflow
Heap-based buffer overflow in **`ngx_http_proxy_v2_module`** and **`ngx_http_grpc_module`**, triggered when `proxy_http_version` is set to **2** or `grpc_pass` is used to proxy **HTTP/2** traffic.
- Fixed in NGINX Open Source **1.30.3 / 1.31.2**, NGINX Plus **R37 P2.1 (37.0.2.1)** and **R36 P6**.
- Mitigation: remove `ignore_invalid_headers off`; reduce `large_client_header_buffers` size below 2 MB.

## Defender actions
- Patch to NGINX OSS 1.31.2 (or 1.30.3 for the HTTP/2 fix) / NGINX Plus R37 P2.1 / R36 P6 immediately.
- If patching is delayed: disable HTTP/3 (42530) and apply the HTTP/2 config mitigations (42055).
- Inventory edge/reverse-proxy NGINX instances using HTTP/3 or HTTP/2 upstream proxying — those are the exposed configs.

## Sources
> Source: [@TheHackersNews (X) — F5 Patches Two Critical NGINX Open Source Flaws](https://x.com/TheHackersNews/status/2067661885907030116) — 2026-06-18

- SecurityWeek: https://www.securityweek.com/f5-patches-critical-high-severity-nginx-vulnerabilities/

## Update — 2026-06-22 (clearer technical path)
The Hacker News published a follow-up clarifying the exploit mechanics of both flaws:
- **CVE-2026-42530** "comes down to an **HTTP/3 lifetime mismatch** that can leave a **freed stream pointer treated as valid**" — i.e., the use-after-free arises because a QUIC/HTTP/3 stream object is freed but a dangling reference continues to be used as if live.
- **CVE-2026-42055** "lets **oversized HPACK data write past its buffer**, causing [an] unauthenticated worker" overflow — confirming the HTTP/2 heap overflow is reachable pre-auth via crafted HPACK (header-compression) data exceeding buffer bounds.

No change to remediation: patch to NGINX OSS 1.31.2 (HTTP/3) / 1.30.3 (HTTP/2) or NGINX Plus R37 P2.1 / R36 P6; disable HTTP/3 and apply HTTP/2 config mitigations if patching is delayed.

# CVE-2026-46316 — Linux Kernel KVM Guest-to-Host Escape (arm64)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

## Summary
A **critical Linux kernel vulnerability** (**CVE-2026-46316**) enables a **guest-to-host escape** in **KVM environments on arm64 systems**. A proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit has been publicly released. Because the flaw lives in the in-kernel KVM implementation (not user-space components like QEMU), successful exploitation results in **direct compromise of the host kernel** rather than a confined user-space process — making it especially severe for multi-tenant / cloud arm64 hosts.

## Details
- **CVE:** CVE-2026-46316
- **Affected:** In-kernel KVM implementation on **arm64** (not QEMU/user-space)
- **Root cause:** Race condition in the **vGIC-ITS (Interrupt Translation Service) emulation** within KVM on arm64
- **Impact:** Guest VM → host kernel escape (full host compromise)
- **Discoverer:** Security researcher **Hyunwoo Kim (V4bel)**
- **PoC:** Publicly released (per source)

## Why It Matters
- Direct host-kernel compromise breaks the core VM isolation boundary
- arm64 server/cloud fleets (increasingly common) are exposed
- Public PoC lowers the bar for weaponization

## Recommended Actions
- Identify arm64 hosts running KVM with untrusted/multi-tenant guests
- Apply kernel updates addressing CVE-2026-46316 as soon as available from your distro

# CVE-2026-50548 / CVE-2026-50549 — Cursor IDE "DuneSlide" Zero-Click Prompt-Injection RCE

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical — CVSS **9.8** (both).
**Component:** Cursor AI code editor / IDE (all versions **before 3.0**).
**Type:** Zero-click prompt injection → sandbox escape → **OS-level remote code execution**.
**Research name:** "DuneSlide" (Cato AI Labs).

## Summary
Two critical RCE flaws in the Cursor AI IDE allow a **zero-click prompt-injection** attack to break out of Cursor's sandbox and run arbitrary code on the host OS. An attacker who can get injected instructions in front of the agent (e.g., poisoned repo content, MCP data, web content the agent reads) can overwrite critical system files such as the `cursorsandbox` binary, converting sandboxed commands into **unsandboxed RCE** and leading to full compromise of the host and connected SaaS workspaces. Cursor's maker states >50% of the Fortune 500 use the tool.

## Technical Detail
- **CVE-2026-50548:** The sandbox permits writes into a command's working folder. That folder is the optional `working_directory` parameter on Cursor's `run_terminal_cmd` tool; when the agent sets it to a non-default path, Cursor adds that path to the allowed-write list without validation.
- **CVE-2026-50549:** Before writing, Cursor resolves symlinks to confirm the real destination is inside the project. The bug is the fallback: when the check fails (target doesn't exist, or attacker removes read access from a path component), Cursor trusts the shortcut's in-project path instead — enabling writes outside the project.

## Recommended Actions
- Upgrade to **Cursor 3.0** (fix released 2026-04-02); every prior version is affected.
- Treat all agent-readable content (repos, MCP servers, fetched web pages) as untrusted prompt-injection surface.
- Constrain agent file-write scope and monitor for writes to sandbox/runtime binaries.

CVE-2026-54121.body:
# CVE-2026-54121 "Certighost" — Low-Privileged AD User Coerces Enterprise CA into Issuing a Domain Controller Certificate

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Type:** CVE / AD CS privilege escalation → domain takeover | **Severity:** Critical (domain compromise) | **Date:** 2026-08-17 (analysis published)

## Summary
**Certighost (CVE-2026-54121)** allows a **low-privileged Active Directory user holding nothing more than a standard domain account** to coerce an **Enterprise Certification Authority (AD CS)** into issuing a valid **authentication certificate for a Domain Controller** — and then use that certificate to **authenticate as the Domain Controller**.

A working **proof-of-concept was published on 24 July 2026**. Microsoft has shipped a fix.

## Why This Class of Bug Keeps Recurring
The Certification Authority is the most over-trusted, under-managed component in most mature AD estates. When the CA signs a certificate, **every machine, service, and authentication flow downstream treats that signature as truth**. Organisations typically deploy the CA once and never revisit it — no template review, no enrolment auditing, no tiering.

Certighost sits in the same family as ESC1–ESC16 / Certifried (CVE-2022-26923): the recurring theme is that **certificate enrolment is an authentication-material issuing pipeline**, and anyone who can influence what goes into a certificate can influence who they are allowed to be. Standard domain user → Domain Controller is the maximum-severity outcome of that pattern.

## Attack Path (conceptual)
1. Attacker holds any standard domain account (no special rights).
2. Coerces the Enterprise CA into issuing an authentication certificate whose subject/SAN identifies a **Domain Controller**.
3. Uses that certificate for PKINIT/Schannel authentication as the DC machine account.
4. DC-level identity → DCSync, full directory compromise, golden-ticket-equivalent persistence.

See also: [[DCSync-Attack-Steal-AD-Password-Hashes-DRSUAPI-2026]] — the natural follow-on once DC identity is obtained.

## Action
- **Apply the Microsoft patch** across all AD CS servers and domain controllers.
- Audit certificate templates: enrolment permissions, whether requesters can supply subject/SAN, and manager-approval requirements.
- Enable and **centrally collect AD CS auditing** (certificate issuance events) — most environments have this off, which is why these attacks go unnoticed.
- Hunt for issued certificates whose subject or SAN references a **Domain Controller or machine account** but whose requester was a standard user.
- Treat the CA as **Tier 0**: same isolation, admin-workstation discipline, and monitoring as domain controllers.
- Consider tooling (e.g. Certipy/Certify-class assessment) to enumerate misconfigured templates before an attacker does.

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/certighost-and-the-privilege-hiding-in-your-certificate-authority/) — Mon, 17 Aug 2026 (authored by Len Noe, BeyondTrust)

- Look for unusual ViewState-based POST requests on LMS endpoints

# CVE-2026-55200 — libssh2 Out-of-Bounds Heap Write (SSH Client RCE)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical — CVSS **9.2** (per VulnCheck, as reported)
**Affected:** **libssh2** SSH client library — **every version up to and including 1.11.1**. libssh2 is embedded in a very large number of tools, language bindings, and applications that make outbound SSH connections.
**Type:** **Out-of-bounds heap write** in `ssh2_transport_read()` (transport-layer packet parsing) → memory corruption, potential remote code execution.
**Status:** Reported; verify availability of a fixed release (expected >1.11.1) and patch.

## Summary
A critical memory-corruption flaw was reported in **libssh2**, the widely embedded client-side SSH library. The bug is an **out-of-bounds heap write in `ssh2_transport_read()`**, the routine that parses incoming SSH transport packets. Because the defect is in client-side packet handling, a **malicious or compromised SSH server** (or an active man-in-the-middle) can send crafted transport data to a connecting client and corrupt heap memory — a primitive that can escalate to **remote code execution** in the process linking libssh2. The library's ubiquity (git tooling, language bindings, automation agents, network/management software) makes the blast radius broad.

## Why it matters
- Client-side trigger: any tool that connects out to an attacker-controlled or hijacked SSH endpoint is exposed.
- "Embedded in countless tools" — transitive dependency risk means many products ship libssh2 without it being obvious.

## Defender actions
- Inventory software and dependencies that bundle or link **libssh2**; identify versions **≤ 1.11.1**.
- Update libssh2 to the fixed release once published; rebuild/repackage downstream software that statically links it.
- Until patched, avoid connecting libssh2-based clients to untrusted SSH servers; pin known-good host keys to reduce MitM risk.
- Watch vendor advisories for products that embed libssh2 (git clients, automation/CI agents, network management tools).

## Sources

# CVE-2026-57433 — Perl Storable Deserialization Integer Overflow (CVSS 9.8)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** Critical — CVSS 9.8, no authentication required
**Affected:** Perl **Storable** module, versions **prior to 3.41**
**Type:** Signed integer overflow in **`SX_HOOK` deserialization** via `retrieve_hook_common`
**Fix:** Upgrade Storable to **3.41**

## Summary
A critical vulnerability, **CVE-2026-57433**, affects Perl's **Storable** serialization module in versions **before 3.41**. The flaw is a **signed integer overflow in `SX_HOOK` deserialization**, reachable through **`retrieve_hook_common`** when Storable deserializes untrusted (attacker-controlled) frozen data. Because Storable is widely embedded in Perl applications and caching/session layers that deserialize external input, an attacker who can supply crafted serialized data may corrupt memory — hence the CVSS 9.8 / no-auth rating.

## Why it matters
- Storable is a core Perl serialization primitive; many apps `thaw()`/`retrieve()` data that ultimately originates from untrusted sources (caches, queues, uploaded blobs, cross-service messages).
- Deserialization memory-corruption bugs frequently escalate from crash to code execution.

## Defender / researcher actions
- **Upgrade Storable to 3.41** across all Perl environments.
- Audit code paths that `thaw`/`retrieve` externally-influenced data; never deserialize untrusted Storable blobs.
- For bug bounty: hunt Perl services (legacy web apps, mail/AV stacks, monitoring agents) that accept serialized input.

## Sources

# CVE-2026-60004 — Gitea `diffpatch` Code Injection → RCE (KEV, Exploited ITW)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical (code injection → remote code execution) — **actively exploited**
**Component:** Gitea self-hosted Git service
**Fixed in:** **1.27.1** (released late July 2026)
**KEV added:** 2026-08-25 · **FCEB remediation deadline: 2026-08-28**

## Details
Gitea contains a **code injection** flaw reachable via the **`diffpatch` API endpoint**. An attacker holding **repository write access** can submit a malicious patch that plants an **executable Git hook**, which then runs shell commands as the **Gitea service account**.

- **Exploitation observed:** a developer reported their Gitea instance targeted by an unknown actor deploying a **cryptocurrency-miner-like dropper**.
- **Exposure:** Shadowserver tracks **~5,000 Gitea instances exposed to the internet**.
- CISA added the CVE to KEV on 25 Aug 2026 and issued a **3-day** federal patch deadline (28 Aug).
- CCCS issued a parallel **Gitea security advisory AV26-845** (25 Aug 2026).

## Precondition caveat (record of nuance)
The vulnerability requires **repository write access**, not pure unauthenticated access. Several syndicated write-ups describe it as "unauthenticated attackers read server files and gain RCE" — that framing conflicts with the CISA/vendor description and appears to conflate this bug with a separate file-read issue. **Treat the write-access precondition as the authoritative one** until Gitea publishes a fuller advisory.

## Action
- Upgrade to **Gitea ≥ 1.27.1** immediately.
- Audit `.git/hooks` across all repositories for unexpected executable hooks.
- Review the Gitea service account for spawned processes / miner artefacts.
- Restrict who holds repository write access; treat write access as an RCE-equivalent privilege on unpatched instances.
- Remove Gitea instances from direct internet exposure.

## Related
- [[CVE-2026-20896-Gitea-Docker-XWEBAUTHUSER-Header-Spoof]] — separate Gitea auth-bypass exploited ITW in July 2026. **Two independently exploited Gitea flaws in ~6 weeks.**

> Source: [CISA KEV Alert](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/08/25/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog) — 2026-08-25
> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-gitea-rce-actively-exploited.html) — 2026-08-26
> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-now-exploit-critical-gitea-flaw-in-code-injection-attacks/) — 2026-08-26

## Tags
#cve #gitea #code-injection #rce #git-hooks #kev #exploited-itw #supply-chain #verified

---

## Update — 2026-08-28: 8,300+ servers still vulnerable, three days after the KEV deadline

BleepingComputer reports **over 8,300 Gitea servers remain vulnerable** to code-execution attacks.

Timeline against that number:
- **late July 2026** — fixed in **1.27.1**
- **2026-08-25** — added to **CISA KEV**; FCEB remediation deadline **2026-08-28**
- **2026-08-28** — **8,300+ still exposed**, on the deadline day itself

Compare the Shadowserver figure of **~5,000 exposed instances** recorded in this note on 2026-08-26. The count reported has **gone up, not down** — most likely a scope/methodology difference between Shadowserver's exposed-instance count and BleepingComputer's vulnerable-server count rather than genuine growth in exposure, but **the discrepancy is recorded rather than reconciled**, since no source explains it.

Either way the remediation direction is not visibly downward a month after a patch existed and three days after a federal deadline.

This is now the concrete data point behind the week's **edge-exposure convergence** — see `Guides/Edge-Device-Exposure-Convergence-NCSC-Tenable-Microsoft-2026-08-27.md`.

**Action:** re-scan. Do not assume a patch instruction issued is a patch applied.

CVE-2026-61979.body:
# CVE-2026-61979 + CVE-2026-15981 — miniOrange SAML 2.0 SSO for WordPress — Auth Bypass Chain, Exploited

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-target-wordpress-sites-in-miniorange-auth-bypass-attacks/) — Mon, 24 Aug 2026 19:26 UTC
> Also: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/attackers-target-miniorange-saml-flaws.html); SC Media

## The chain — two bugs that compose
**CVE-2026-61979 (CVSS 8.1)** — *signature algorithm confusion*. The plugin takes the signature algorithm **from the incoming SAML response** rather than enforcing the configured one. An attacker selects **HMAC-SHA1**, which causes the plugin to treat the IdP's **RSA public key as the shared HMAC secret**. The public key is, by definition, public — so the attacker can forge a valid signature.

**CVE-2026-15981 (CVSS 9.8)** — *malformed signatures accepted as valid*. The plugin misreads **OpenSSL verification errors as successful validation**.

Chained, these yield **administrator session cookies** without credentials.

## Exploitation
**DigitalOcean detected an anomaly on 16 Aug 2026**; analysis confirmed both CVEs used against the **free edition, version 16.1.9**.

## Fixed in
- CVE-2026-61979 → **17.0.5** (Standard edition)
- CVE-2026-15981 → **17.0.6** (Standard edition)

Update to the latest `miniorange-saml-20-single-sign-on`, or disable the plugin until patched and validated.

## Note on CVE numbering — unsettled
Syndicated coverage also circulates **CVE-2026-15013** and **CVE-2026-57807** against miniOrange SSO products. Those appear to be **different plugins in the same vendor family** (SAML SSO Login / OAuth SSO), not this pair. THN and BleepingComputer both name **61979 + 15981** for this exploitation event; those are recorded here as primary. Treat the other two as unconfirmed for this incident.

## Why it's worth attention
A WordPress plugin is a low-prestige target, but this one **federates WordPress to corporate identity platforms**. Admin takeover of the WP site is the floor, not the ceiling — the interesting question is what else trusts that IdP relationship.

## Detection
- SAML responses specifying **HMAC-SHA1** where the configured algorithm is RSA-SHA256.
- Admin logins with a SAML assertion but **no corresponding IdP-side authentication event**.

# CVE-2026-63030 — WordPress Core "wp2shell" Pre-Authentication RCE

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 7 independent sources

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS pending, pre-auth RCE) | **Date:** 2026-07-17

## Summary
A critical **pre-authentication remote code execution** vulnerability dubbed **wp2shell** was disclosed in **WordPress Core**. A single anonymous HTTP request can run code on an unpatched **WordPress 6.9–7.0.1** site — **even a default install with zero plugins**. The flaw chains a **REST API batch route confusion** (`/wp-json/batch/v1`) with a **SQL injection**, requiring no login, no special configuration, and no plugins.

## Key details
- **CVE:** CVE-2026-63030 (critical pre-auth RCE); companion **CVE-2026-60137** (high-severity) fixed in the same release.
- **Affected:** WordPress core **6.9.0–6.9.4** and **7.0.0–7.0.1**.
- **Fixed:** Emergency security releases **7.0.2** and **6.9.5**, published **2026-07-17**.
- **Root cause:** REST **batch API** route confusion → SQL injection → code execution. Reachable pre-auth on default installs.
- **Discovery:** Adam Kues, **Assetnote / Searchlight Cyber**.
- **Public test:** `https://wp2shell.com/` (checks if an instance is vulnerable).
- **Exploitation:** No in-the-wild exploitation observed at disclosure (per Searchlight Cyber), but mass scanning expected given default-install reachability and no CVE-signature yet for legacy scanners.

## Action / Mitigation
- **Update immediately** to WordPress **7.0.2** (or **6.9.5** on the 6.9 branch).
- If patching is delayed: block anonymous access to the batch API — block `/wp-json/batch/v1` and `?rest_route=/batch/v1` at the WAF, or install a plugin restricting anonymous REST access.
- Hunt web logs for POSTs to the batch route from unauthenticated sources; review for SQLi-style payloads.

- https://slcyber.io/research-center/wp2shell-pre-authentication-rce-in-wordpress-core/

# CVE-2026-63219 + CVE-2026-58400 — GeoNetwork Unauthenticated RCE Chain (Government Geoportal Backends)

⚠️ **Verification:** Single source — Ethiack / Rafael Castilho, relayed by The Hacker News, quoting the upstream GeoNetwork advisory. Exposure figures are vendor-single-sourced.

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical | **Date logged:** 2026-09-02
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-63219 (CVSS 8.6), CVE-2026-58400 (CVSS 9.1)
**Fixed:** 4.4.12 and 4.2.17, shipped 2026-07-08
**Details published:** 2026-08-31
**Exploitation:** None reported

## Summary

Two GeoNetwork flaws chain into **unauthenticated remote code execution** on the open-source geospatial metadata catalog that sits behind many government geoportals — including the backend of the European **INSPIRE** geoportal. Patches shipped 2026-07-08; details went public 2026-08-31.

## The chain

| CVE | CVSS | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-63219** | 8.6 | **Missing authorization check** on the formatter upload endpoint. An unauthenticated user can write arbitrary `.xsl` or `.zip` formatter files into the GeoNetwork formatter directory. |
| **CVE-2026-58400** | 9.1 | **Unsafe configuration of the Saxon XSLT processor** used to render formatters. A loaded stylesheet can call `java.lang.Runtime.exec()` or `java.lang.ProcessBuilder` and run OS commands as the GeoNetwork process user. |

**Attack path:** upload a malicious formatter through the unprotected endpoint → issue a follow-up `GET` to any public record → Saxon executes the stylesheet → code execution.

CVE-2026-58400 alone is scored as requiring high privileges, because you need upload rights. **CVE-2026-63219 removes that precondition entirely.** That is the whole story: two individually survivable bugs compose into pre-auth RCE, and neither one's CVSS describes the result.

## Regression origin

Ethiack reports the chain is reachable **starting at version 4.0.6**, when the formatter endpoint was refactored and the authorization line was dropped. This is a deleted-line regression, not a design flaw — which means it is the kind of thing a diff-aware test would have caught and a scanner would not.

## Read the exposure figure precisely

Ethiack fingerprinted **121 internet-exposed deployments running affected versions across 39 countries**, of which it says **89% were government-, military- or national-agency-related**.

⚠️ That describes *exposed instances running vulnerable versions* — **not confirmed victims, and not compromises** — and the fingerprinting is single-sourced to the reporting vendor. Same document-class discipline this vault applies to leak-site claims: **a scan count is evidence of exposure, never of intrusion.**

## Action

1. Upgrade to **4.4.12** or **4.2.17**.
2. If you cannot patch immediately, **block unauthenticated access to the formatter upload endpoint** at the reverse proxy.
3. **Hunt retroactively.** Patches shipped 2026-07-08 but details went public 2026-08-31 — any instance still on an affected version has an ~8-week exposure window with a public write-up now available. Look for unexpected `.xsl` / `.zip` files in the formatter directory and for child processes spawned by the GeoNetwork JVM.
4. Execution is as the GeoNetwork process user — review what that account reaches, starting with database credentials and catalog storage.

## Open questions

- No exploitation in the wild reported; no IOCs published.
- **The article's description of the Saxon configuration reads as internally contradictory** — it states secure processing is enabled and extension functions disabled, then describes extension functions executing. Confirm the exact unsafe setting against the upstream GeoNetwork advisory before building detections on it.

# CVE-2026-64849 — MLflow Webhook DNS-Rebinding SSRF, Unauthenticated (CISA KEV, Actively Exploited)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-warns-of-hackers-exploiting-critical-mlflow-vulnerability/) — 2026-08-20 | [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/) 2026-08-18 | Primary: **CISA KEV**


**Type:** CVE / SSRF via DNS rebinding → cloud credential theft | **Severity:** Critical | **Date:** 2026-08-18/20

## Summary
**CVE-2026-64849** — a **DNS-rebinding SSRF bypass in MLflow's outbound webhook delivery**, patched in **MLflow 3.15.0**. **CISA added it to the KEV catalog** and warned federal agencies of active exploitation.

MLflow is a Linux Foundation-backed open-source AI/LLM engineering platform with **30M+ monthly downloads**, used to debug, evaluate, optimise and monitor AI applications.

## Root Cause
The **default MLflow Tracking Server** (`mlflow server`, **no authentication**, default SQLite backend) **exposes the model-registry webhooks API unauthenticated** — including a **synchronous `POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test`** endpoint that **returns the upstream response status and body to the caller**.

That last property is what turns a blind SSRF into a fully readable one. Combined with a **DNS-rebinding bypass** of the outbound SSRF guard, an unprivileged remote attacker can reach:
- Internal-only services on the server's network
- **Cloud instance metadata endpoints** (IMDS) → cloud credentials and secrets

## Why This Class Keeps Recurring
This is the same shape as **CVE-2025-62593 (Ray)**, added to KEV on 2026-08-17 — an AI/ML platform that ships **insecure-by-default, unauthenticated** and gets exposed to networks its designers never assumed. See `CVE-2025-62593-Ray-DNS-Rebinding-Browser-RCE-KEV-Exploited.md`. Two DNS-rebinding-based KEV entries against ML tooling **inside four days** is a pattern, not a coincidence: ML platforms are being treated as internal dev tools while sitting on production cloud credentials.

## Action
1. **Upgrade MLflow to 3.15.0 or later.**
2. **Never expose a Tracking Server to untrusted networks without authentication** — the default configuration has no auth at all.
3. Enforce **IMDSv2** (or the cloud equivalent requiring a PUT-obtained token) so an SSRF cannot trivially read instance credentials.
4. Apply **egress filtering** from ML infrastructure; deny outbound to link-local `169.254.169.254`.
5. If exposed and unpatched: assume credential compromise — **rotate any cloud role credentials reachable from the host** and review CloudTrail / audit logs for use of those credentials.
6. Federal agencies: KEV remediation deadlines apply.

# CVE-2026-65643 — cPanel & WHM: Parked / Addon Domain Handling → Arbitrary File Write → Root Code Execution

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical (vendor rating)
**Affected:** **All supported versions** of cPanel & WHM
**Precondition:** an **authenticated account holder** who can add **parked or addon domains** — i.e. an ordinary hosting customer

## Mechanism
An authenticated account holder able to add a parked or addon domain can **create arbitrary files on the server**. cPanel states plainly: *successful exploitation leads to code execution as the root user, giving an attacker full control of the server.*

## Why the low bar matters
The privilege required is the privilege every shared-hosting customer already has. On a shared cPanel box this is a **single-tenant-to-whole-server** escalation: one customer account — bought for a few dollars, or taken over via a weak password — becomes root over every other tenant on the machine. For hosting providers this is a **multi-tenant isolation failure**, not a customer-side patch item.

## Patched versions
- 11.110.0.141 or later
- 11.134.0.53 or later
- 11.136.0.37 or later
- 11.138.0.2 or later
- 11.138.1.7 or later (**WP Squared**)

⚠️ The notification names **WP Squared** in the patched list and **does not mention DNSOnly**. DNSOnly operators should seek explicit vendor confirmation rather than assume coverage.

Note: cPanel patched three separate flaws in July 2026, and the fixed builds named in those advisories overlap this line — verify the running build number rather than assuming the July update covered this.

## Action
1. Patch to the listed builds immediately. Verify with `/usr/local/cpanel/cpanel -V`, not from memory of the last update.
2. Hosting providers: audit for unexpected root-owned files with recent mtimes, new cron entries, and modified system binaries created around domain-add operations.
3. Review parked/addon domain creation logs for anomalous entries.
4. Assume shared-tenant compromise where the box was unpatched and any account was untrusted.

# CVE-2026-66066 — Ruby on Rails Active Storage "KindaRails2Shell" (libvips) Arbitrary File Read → RCE

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**CVSSv4:** 9.5 (Critical) — CWE-1188 (Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default)
**Disclosed:** Rails security advisory 2026-07-29; press coverage 2026-08-01. Full details embargoed until no later than 2026-08-28.

## Summary
A critical vulnerability in Rails **Active Storage** image processing when used with the **libvips** image-processing library. An **unauthenticated** attacker who can submit an image upload to an affected app can read arbitrary files accessible to the Rails application process. Exposed secrets (credentials, tokens, `secret_key_base`) can then be leveraged to achieve **remote code execution** or lateral movement to connected systems. Dubbed **KindaRails2Shell** by Rapid7.

## Affected / Fixed
- Vulnerable when the app uses **libvips** for Active Storage image processing **and** accepts image uploads from untrusted users.
- Affected: Active Storage **< 7.2.3.2**, **8.0.x < 8.0.5.1**, **8.1.x < 8.1.3.1**.
- Fixed: **7.2.3.2 / 8.0.5.1 / 8.1.3.1**. Confirm **libvips ≥ 8.13**.

## Mitigation
- Patch to the fixed Active Storage release; then **rotate every secret the app can read**.
- On libvips ≥ 8.13: set env `VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED` or call `Vips.block_untrusted(true)` (ruby-vips ≥ 2.2.1) to temporarily disable the vulnerable path.

## Bug-bounty / pentest relevance
Test any Rails target that accepts image uploads (avatars, attachments) and uses `image_processing`/libvips. File-read primitive → grab `config/master.key` / `secret_key_base` → forge cookies / deserialization → RCE. Embargoed technical detail (≤ Aug 28) means a PoC window is likely imminent.

> Source: [BleepingComputer — Rails patches critical Active Storage flaw with RCE potential](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/rails-patches-critical-active-storage-flaw-with-rce-potential/) — 2026-08-01
> Source: [Rapid7 — KindaRails2Shell CVE-2026-66066](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-kindarails2shell-cve-2026-66066-critical-arbitrary-file-read-and-possible-remote-code-execution-in-ruby-on-rails/)
> Source: [The Hacker News — Critical Rails Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Read Server Files](https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-rails-flaw-could-let.html)

## Tags
 #verified


---

## Update — 2026-09-01: exploited in the wild, with C2 established

⚠️ **Single primary source** — VulnCheck, via The Hacker News.

**The PoC window this note predicted on 2026-08-01 has closed.** VulnCheck reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-66066 alongside Langflow **CVE-2026-0768**, and states that **observed activity established C2**. That is past scanning and past opportunistic file-read — it is a foothold.

### What this changes about the action list
The existing guidance stands, but the ordering inverts. **Rotation is now the remediation and patching is only prevention of the next one.** Any internet-reachable Rails app that used libvips for Active Storage image processing before patching should be treated as having disclosed `secret_key_base`, the master key, database passwords, cloud-storage credentials and API tokens — because that is precisely what the primitive yields and the source says attackers are collecting.

Add to the hunt: **outbound C2 from application servers**, not just evidence of the file-read itself. A successful read leaves little; the C2 does.

⚠️ Still not published in the source read: IOCs, C2 infrastructure, affected version ranges beyond what this note already carries, or a CISA KEV entry.

Filed the same day as `Threat_Intel/CVEs/2026/Critical/CVE-2026-0768-Langflow-Unauth-Python-Code-Execution-Exploited.md` — the two were reported together by VulnCheck as concurrent credential-probing campaigns.

# CVE-2026-66902 — Google::Auth (Perl) OS Command Injection via external_account credentials

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Type:** OS command injection (CWE-78 / CWE-829) | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 9.8) | **Date:** 2026-08-05

## Summary
**Google::Auth** versions **before 0.06** for **Perl** run a command named in an `external_account` credentials JSON via an **ungated `system()` call**. Any actor who can supply or modify the credentials JSON can inject code that runs as the process loading the credentials.

## Technical Detail
- The **Pluggable** subclass reads `credential_source.executable.command` from the credentials JSON and runs it as `system($command)` — a **single-argument** call, so the whole string is passed to `/bin/sh -c`.
- The `environment_variables` map from the same JSON is copied into `%ENV` first.
- Path is reached from the standard **Application Default Credentials (ADC)** flow, including a `"type": "external_account"` config read from the file named by `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.

## Impact
Code execution as the loading process wherever an attacker-controlled or attacker-modifiable ADC file is honored (CI runners, misconfigured service accounts, shared credential paths).

## Fix
- Upgrade to **Google-Auth ≥ 0.06**, which now **throws unless** `GOOGLE_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_EXECUTABLES=1` is set.
- Audit for untrusted/writable `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` paths.

> Source: [oss-sec advisory](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/435) — 2026-08-05 (via @SecAlertsCo, X feed)

# CVE-2026-66909 — Apache CXF JMS ObjectMessage Deserialization RCE

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical (CVSS 9.8)
**Status:** Patched
**Date captured:** 2026-08-08

## Summary
Apache CXF's JMS transport deserializes the body of any inbound JMS `ObjectMessage` using native Java deserialization with **zero type restrictions**. Any attacker able to place a message on the service's JMS destination can submit a malicious serialized object — leading to denial of service or, if a suitable gadget class is on the classpath, **remote code execution**. No authentication beyond the ability to write to the queue is required.

## Affected / Fixed
- Fixed in Apache CXF **4.2.3**, **4.1.8**, and **3.6.12**.
- The fix disables `ObjectMessage` deserialization by default, with a config switch to re-enable if needed.

## Remediation
- Upgrade to a fixed version immediately.
- Restrict who can write to the JMS destination; do not expose broker queues to untrusted producers.
- Audit classpath for known deserialization gadget chains.

# CVE-2026-69836 — Microsoft Entra ID Deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0, Exploited in the Wild)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 5 independent sources

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/microsoft-entra-id-flaw-cvss-100.html) — 2026-08-21 | Corroborated: [Cyber Security News](https://cybersecuritynews.com/entra-id-rce-vulnerability-exploited/) 2026-08-21


**Type:** CVE / unsafe deserialization → unauthenticated RCE | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 10.0) | **Date:** 2026-08-20/21

## Summary
Microsoft disclosed **CVE-2026-69836 (CVSS 10.0)** in **Entra ID** (formerly Azure AD / Azure Active Directory) — **deserialization of untrusted data allowing an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network**. Microsoft states the flaw **has been exploited in the wild** but that it is **"fully mitigated"** service-side and **no customer action is required**.

Credited to Microsoft Principal Security Engineer **Robert Fitzpatrick**.

## Why This Matters More Than the "No Action Required" Line Suggests
A CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE in the **identity plane** of a hyperscale cloud is about as high-consequence as a cloud vulnerability gets. Entra ID is the trust root for token issuance across M365, Azure, and every federated SaaS app behind it. Code execution there is not a tenant-scoped problem in the way a customer-side bug is.

**Microsoft has published no detail on:**
- How the vulnerability was exploited
- When exploitation began
- Whether it is still ongoing
- How it was discovered

"Fully mitigated, no action required" resolves the *patching* question. It does not resolve the **assurance** question — customers cannot independently scope blast radius without the timeline.

## Detection / Response Guidance (defensive, service-side flaw)
Because customers cannot patch a service-side flaw, the useful work is **retrospective hunting**:
- Review **Entra ID sign-in logs** and **audit logs** for anomalous service-principal and application activity, unusual token issuance, and consent grants.
- Hunt for **unexpected application registrations, credential (secret/certificate) additions to existing service principals**, and role assignment changes.
- Check for **federation/domain trust modifications** (a classic post-identity-compromise persistence path).
- Review **Risk Detections** and privileged role activations over the widest log-retention window available.
- SANS ISC published a timely Graph + PowerShell series this same week that is directly applicable — see the *Related* section.

## Related

- **No patching action available** — service-side, vendor-mitigated.
- **Do** run a retrospective Entra ID audit-log hunt as above.

## Enrichment — Verified 2026-08-21

> Corroborated across [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/microsoft-entra-id-flaw-cvss-100.html), [Cyber Security News](https://cybersecuritynews.com/entra-id-rce-vulnerability-exploited/), [Cyberpress](https://cyberpress.org/critical-microsoft-entra-id-rce-flaw/) and [CrowdStrike's August 2026 Patch Tuesday analysis](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/patch-tuesday-analysis-august-2026/).

- **Weakness class: CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data).** Entra ID's backend processes specially crafted serialised objects without proper validation; an attacker sends malicious serialised data to a vulnerable endpoint and executes arbitrary code — **no authentication and no user interaction required** (consistent with the CVSS 10.0).
- **This is a "cloud service CVE."** Microsoft publishes these for transparency on flaws it has already fixed in its own infrastructure. **There is no update package and no KB article** — nothing exists for a customer to deploy. That is why the advisory reads as "no action required" despite the score.
- The distinction matters for reporting: this CVE will appear in vulnerability-management feeds but **cannot be closed by patching**, and will otherwise sit open in a scanner-driven workflow forever. Record it as **vendor-remediated / not-applicable-to-endpoint** with a note, and keep the retrospective log hunt as the actual work item.
- **Correction to initial note:** researcher name is **Robert Fitzpatrick** (THN's original text contained a typo, "Fitzaptrick").

The exploitation timeline gap remains unresolved across all sources.

## Update — 2026-08-23 sweep: **Microsoft REVERSED the exploitation status**

> Source: [Cyber Security News (@The_Cyber_News, X `2090965075620409674`)](https://x.com/The_Cyber_News/status/2090965075620409674) — Sat, 22 Aug 2026 00:51 UTC
> Source: [SOCRadar](https://socradar.io/blog/cve-2026-69836-microsoft-entra-id-rce/), [Cybersecurity Dive](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/microsoft-maximum-severity-flaw-entra-id-exploitation/828501/), [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/21/microsoft-entra-id-vulnerability-cve-2026-69836/) — web-verified 2026-08-23

**Microsoft changed the "Exploited" field in its security bulletin from "Yes" to "No" on 21 August 2026**, stating "this vulnerability was not exploited in the wild." **No explanation for the reversal was provided.**

### What this changes in this note
Every "exploited in the wild" statement above — including the note title and the original THN/BleepingComputer/X sourcing — reflects **Microsoft's original bulletin**, which Microsoft has since retracted. The technical facts are unchanged and still stand:
- CVSS **10.0**, **CWE-502** deserialization of untrusted data.
- Cloud-service CVE — **no KB, no update package, nothing for customers to patch**.
- Microsoft states it was **fully mitigated before public disclosure**; no customer action required.
- Researcher credit: **Robert Fitzpatrick**.

### The lesson worth keeping
The vault recorded this as actively exploited across **three independent intake paths in one sweep** (X bookmarks, X feed, THN RSS) — all of which were downstream of a single upstream authority that was wrong. **Source count is not source independence.** When every source traces to one vendor bulletin, confidence should be capped at that bulletin's reliability, and a status reversal should be treated as a live possibility until a second, non-derivative source (a victim, an IR firm, a government advisory) confirms exploitation.

**Filename retained** for link stability; treat the "-Exploited" suffix as historical. Status is now: **critical, mitigated, not exploited.**

# CVE-2026-72529 / CVE-2026-72530 — TrueConf Server Unauthenticated RCE + Sandbox Escape (CISA KEV, Actively Exploited)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-orders-feds-to-patch-actively-exploited-trueconf-server-flaws/) — Fri, 21 Aug 2026
> Source: [CISA — Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/08/20/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) — Thu, 20 Aug 2026

**Type:** CVE / KEV addition | **Severity:** Critical | **Status:** Actively exploited

## The Vulnerabilities
| CVE | Effect |
|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-72529** | **Unauthenticated remote code execution on TCP port 4307.** No login required. |
| **CVE-2026-72530** | **Sandbox escape** — run code directly on the host server, outside TrueConf's confinement. |

Chained, these give an unauthenticated network attacker full code execution on the underlying host.

## Why This Note Exists Separately
The vault already tracked this campaign as a supply-chain event (`Threat_Intel/SupplyChain/TrueConf-HeadMare-Trojanized-Installers-PhantomCore-Backdoor-2026.md`, 2026-08-08) **before CVE identifiers existed**. This sweep is the first time the flaws are individually identified and KEV-listed, which changes them from "an unpatched product" into **tracked, deadline-bound remediation items**.

## Exploitation
- **Kaspersky** traced active exploitation to attackers **trojanizing TrueConf client installers** with the **PhantomCore** and **PhantomGraph** backdoors.
- The **Head Mare** hacktivist group is exploiting the bugs to deploy PhantomCore.
- Matches the previously documented behaviour exactly — the earlier note's port-4307 unauthenticated-code-execution description is now CVE-2026-72529.

## Remediation Deadlines (BOD 22-01, US federal)
- **CVE-2026-72529 — due 23 August 2026** (a *three-day* window, unusually short; CISA reserves this for unauthenticated RCE under live exploitation).
- **CVE-2026-72530 — due 2 September 2026.**

Fixed in **5.3.9 / 5.4.9 / 5.5.5** — released **18 June 2026**. The patch has been available for **two months**; this is an exposure problem, not a fix-availability problem.

## Action
1. Inventory TrueConf Server instances. Confirm version ≥ 5.3.9 / 5.4.9 / 5.5.5.
2. **Firewall TCP 4307** from untrusted networks regardless of patch state.
3. Assume any client installer served from an unpatched server is trojanized — re-hash against vendor checksums and re-deploy.
4. Hunt for LSASS access and outbound reverse SSH on hosts that installed the TrueConf client (PhantomGraph tradecraft).
5. The three-day KEV deadline is the signal: treat exposed instances as **already compromised** until proven otherwise.

# CVE-2026-73296 — Microsoft UFO (open-source UI-automation agent framework), CVSS 9.4

⚠️ **Verification:** Single source (@SecAlertsCo / SecAlerts) — **vulnerability class and impact not yet read from a vendor advisory**

**CVSS:** 9.4 (Critical)
**Product:** Microsoft **UFO** — Microsoft's open-source **UI-Focused agent framework** for automating Windows GUI applications with an LLM
**Fix:** Available per SecAlerts

## Why this one matters beyond its score
UFO is an **agentic desktop-automation framework**: it drives real Windows UI with model-generated actions. A critical flaw in that class of software is not a web-app flaw with a bigger number — the exploit primitive is *actions taken on the user's desktop under the user's identity*, which is exactly the boundary that endpoint controls assume is human.

This is the fourth AI-agent-infrastructure item in a single 24-hour window in this vault (Langflow CVE-2026-0768, METR key theft, the SANS free-LLM-endpoint honeypot, and this). **The pattern is that agent frameworks are shipping with the security maturity of pre-2010 web software while holding the privileges of a logged-in user.**

- **The vulnerability class is unknown** from this source. CVSS 9.4 is quoted; the vector is not.
- Affected version range unknown.
- No evidence of exploitation.
- **This note is sourced to an aggregator relaying a CVE record.** Per the standing rule recorded 2026-08-31: record what the document class is. Upgrade this note only against the Microsoft/GitHub advisory.

# CVE-2026-74232 / CVE-2026-74233 — SPEAKINGSTONE and DARKLANTERN: Factory Implants in ZBT Router Firmware

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** Critical — **CVSS 4.0 = 9.3**, **CVSS 3.1 = 9.8**, both vectors: network, **no privileges, no user interaction**
**Vendor:** Shenzhen Zhibotong Electronics (**ZBT**)
**Class:** **Factory-shipped implants** — not accidental vulnerabilities

## The two implants

### SPEAKINGSTONE — CVE-2026-74232
- Runs as the service **`yunmgrd`**.
- **Beacons outbound over UDP port 10000** to a **hardcoded C2 server**.
- Because it dials **outward**, it **works from behind NAT and ordinary egress filtering** — no inbound reachability required, no port forward, no UPnP.
- Protocol message types support:
  - execute **arbitrary commands as root**
  - **exfiltrate the WAN PPPoE username and password**
  - write and read a **DNS hijack** configuration

### DARKLANTERN — CVE-2026-74233
Second, independent implant in the same firmware giving unauthenticated remote root command execution.

## Why this is a different problem from a normal router CVE
This is not a memory-safety bug that an attacker must find and weaponise. It is **functionality the vendor shipped**: a named service, a hardcoded C2, and a message protocol with an exfiltration verb for the subscriber's own PPPoE credentials. The DNS-hijack primitive means an operator of the C2 can silently redirect every name lookup for every device behind the router.

The **outbound-beacon design defeats the standard consumer-router threat model**, which assumes "not exposed to the internet" is sufficient mitigation. It is not — the device initiates the connection.

## Detection
- Egress **UDP/10000** from any consumer/SMB router segment — high-signal, rarely legitimate.
- Presence of the **`yunmgrd`** process on any device you can shell into.
- Unexplained changes to router DNS settings; DNS answers that disagree with an out-of-band resolver.
- ZBT also ships white-label/OEM firmware — **the badge on the case may not say ZBT**. Fingerprint by firmware and service names, not brand.

## Action
- Treat affected devices as **compromised by design**. Replacement, not patching, is the realistic remediation.
- If replacement is not immediate: block UDP/10000 egress upstream, pin DNS to a known resolver enforced at the firewall, and **rotate the PPPoE credentials** — assume they are already known.
- Add ZBT/OEM router presence to supply-chain and third-party risk registers.

## Related
Second consecutive sweep with a China-nexus embedded-device supply-chain finding, alongside the **DoJ/FBI QTFY (QScan / QTRouter) disruption** the same week — see `Threat_Intel/APT_Groups/QTFY/QTFY-Profile.md`.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/china-made-zbt-routers-ship-with-two.html) — 2026-08-28

# CVE-2026-76657 — HPE Networking Fabric Composer API Authentication Bypass (CVSS 10.0)

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 10.0) | **Date logged:** 2026-09-04
**Product:** HPE Networking **Fabric Composer** — API
**Impact:** Unauthenticated attacker obtains **full administrative access**. No credentials required.
**Status:** Patch available. No public exploitation reported at time of logging.

## Summary

**CVE-2026-76657** is an **authentication bypass in the HPE Networking Fabric Composer API** rated **CVSS 10.0**. An unauthenticated attacker reaching the API obtains **full administrative access** to the platform.

## Why a fabric controller is a worse target than a switch

Fabric Composer is the **management and orchestration plane for a data-centre switching fabric** — it does not forward traffic, it decides how traffic is forwarded across every switch it manages. Administrative control of it is therefore a superset of administrative control of the individual devices:

- **Arbitrary re-segmentation.** VLAN, VRF and policy changes made from the controller are legitimate, authorised configuration changes as far as every downstream switch is concerned. There is no exploit signature on the data-plane devices to find.
- **Traffic redirection and mirroring at fabric scale** — a SPAN/ERSPAN destination configured centrally is a passive tap on any segment, invisible to endpoint and application telemetry.
- **It sits below every control that assumes the network is the boundary.** Micro-segmentation, east-west firewalling and zero-trust network policy are all *expressed* through the fabric. Owning the thing that expresses them makes them advisory.

The generalisable point, and one this vault keeps re-deriving: **management planes are consistently under-rated relative to the devices they manage.** A CVSS 10 pre-auth bypass on an orchestrator is not equivalent to a CVSS 10 on one switch; it is that CVSS 10 multiplied by the fabric.

## Action

1. **Patch Fabric Composer immediately** — pre-auth, no credentials, CVSS 10.
2. **Verify the API is not internet-reachable.** It should not be, and for an orchestration plane the honest control is network reachability, not authentication. Confirm rather than assume — verify from outside your own perimeter.
3. **Restrict management-plane access to a dedicated admin network** with its own authentication path, and treat any host that can reach it as a tier-0 asset.
4. **Assume compromise on any instance that was internet-exposed.** Hunt for: new or modified administrative accounts, API tokens issued outside change windows, unexpected configuration pushes, and newly configured mirror/SPAN destinations.
5. **Diff the running fabric configuration against a known-good out-of-band baseline.** Because attacker actions here look like legitimate configuration, configuration diffing is the detection — not log alerting.

## Open questions

- Affected and fixed version ranges not captured in the read — pull from the HPE security bulletin.
- Whether the bypass is reachable on the standard management listener or requires a specific API path.
- No IOCs published.
- Relationship, if any, to the ArubaOS-CX critical RCE patched by HPE the previous day (see `HPE-ArubaOS-CX-Critical-RCE-2026-09.md`) — two critical HPE networking flaws in 48 hours warrants asking whether they came from the same research effort.

## Sources
