CVE-2026-82222.body:
# CVE-2026-82222 — GiveWP WordPress Donation Plugin, Unauthenticated Command Execution

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**CVE:** CVE-2026-82222
**Product:** GiveWP (WordPress donation / fundraising plugin), **100,000+ installs**
**Affected:** through **v4.16.7.1**
**Reported by:** Udin Chan, **2026-07-28**, via **Patchstack**
**Impact:** Arbitrary **OS command execution on the hosting server**

## Root cause — a three-part chain, not a single bug
Patchstack describe exploitation as chaining three distinct issues:

1. An **unsafe helper for unserializing PHP data**
2. A **donation-processing flow that stores attacker-controlled serialized objects**
3. A **gadget chain in libraries bundled with the plugin** that can invoke arbitrary system commands

This is the classic PHP object-injection pattern: untrusted `unserialize()` reached through a business flow that persists attacker data, terminating in a POP gadget available from vendored dependencies.

## Precondition worth reading carefully
BleepingComputer states successful exploitation **depends on the attacker having an account** on the target site. That is a meaningful qualifier — but on a donation platform, **account registration is frequently open by design**, so "authenticated" and "unauthenticated" collapse into the same thing for a large share of installs. Treat the precondition as **weak** unless registration is verifiably closed.

> ⚠️ This is the fourth consecutive sweep in which a published description and the practical attack surface diverge (cf. CVE-2026-8452 DoS-vs-webshell, Gitea preconditions). The standing rule applies: read the vendor text, then read what the exploitation actually requires.

## Action
1. Update GiveWP past **4.16.7.1** immediately.
2. Where update is not possible: **disable open registration**, and put a WAF rule in front of the donation-processing endpoints.
3. Hunt for unexpected child processes of the PHP-FPM / Apache worker on donation sites.
4. Audit bundled library versions — the gadget chain lives in dependencies, so other plugins vendoring the same libraries may be reachable through their own sinks.

> Source: [BleepingComputer — GiveWP WordPress donation plugin flaw lets hackers execute server commands](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/givewp-wordpress-donation-plugin-flaw-lets-hackers-execute-server-commands/) — Fri, 28 Aug 2026

## Tags
#cve-2026-82222 #wordpress #givewp #php-object-injection #deserialization #gadget-chain #patchstack #single-source #unverified

---

## Update 2026-08-30 — CVSS confirmed 10.0, and the precondition above was wrong

Second source obtained: The Hacker News, reporting **Patchstack** and **Wordfence** directly.

**Two corrections to the note above, logged in place rather than edited out.**

**1. The score.** The earlier note recorded "maximum severity" as BleepingComputer's characterisation with no number obtained. The score is **CVSS 10.0**.

**2. The precondition — this is the material correction.** The earlier note recorded BleepingComputer's statement that exploitation *"depends on the attacker having an account"*, and then argued that on a donation platform open registration makes the qualifier weak in practice.

Patchstack's stated condition is different and considerably worse: the site needs **one published donation form and one active payment gateway**. That is not a property of the *attacker*; it is a property of the *site*, and it describes **any GiveWP install that is actually being used for its purpose**. There is no registration state to check and no "authenticated vs unauthenticated" distinction to reason about.

⚠️ **The earlier analysis reached roughly the right operational conclusion — treat the precondition as weak — via reasoning that was wrong.** The recommended mitigation that followed from it, *"disable open registration"*, is **ineffective** and should not be relied on. It is struck here rather than deleted, because the failure mode is the point: an inference chain that lands on a defensible answer can still produce an indefensible control.

**New standing rule:** when an advisory states a precondition, determine whether it constrains the *attacker* or the *target*. Attacker-side preconditions can sometimes be raised by configuration. Target-side preconditions that describe normal operation cannot be mitigated at all — only patched.

## Corrected root cause (Patchstack, verbatim framing)

The chain is a broken "safe unserialize" helper, a donation flow that feeds that helper attacker-controlled data, and a gadget chain in code GiveWP ships. Patchstack's generalisation — worth extracting from the GiveWP specifics — is that PHP object injection reaches RCE when three things line up: somewhere to store an attacker-controlled serialized object, code that later unserializes it, and a gadget chain in loaded classes. Their stated root causes: trusting a serialization sanitizer that does not strip objects, **unserializing data read back from the database as if it were trusted**, and shipping development-only code paths in production.

The transferable finding is the middle one. **Storing attacker data and reading it back does not make it trusted data.**

## Corrected action
1. **Patch past 4.16.7.1. There is no configuration mitigation.**
2. If patching is delayed, the only real controls are a WAF in front of donation-processing endpoints and, failing that, taking the donation form offline.
3. ~~Disable open registration~~ — does not apply; see above.
4. Audit other plugins vendoring the same libraries for reachable gadget chains.

> Source: [The Hacker News — Five Critical WordPress Plugin and Theme Flaws Enable Site Takeover or RCE](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/five-critical-wordpress-plugin-and.html) — 2026-08-29 16:25 UTC

CVE-2026-82329.body:
# CVE-2026-82329 — JFrog Artifactory Authentication Bypass (Admin Token Minting, Exploited)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — watchTowr research relayed by The Hacker News, plus an independent government advisory (CCCS AV26-867)

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical | **Date logged:** 2026-09-02
**CVE:** CVE-2026-82329
**CVSS:** 9.8 (Critical)
**Status:** **Exploited in the wild**, beginning days after public disclosure
**Reported by:** watchTowr

## Summary

An **authentication bypass** in JFrog Artifactory that grants **administrative access under default configurations**. Reporting describes attackers using it to **mint administrative tokens**. Exploitation began days after public disclosure.

## Affected / Fixed

Per CCCS AV26-867, versions **prior to** the following are affected:

`7.111.21` · `7.117.28` · `7.125.20` · `7.133.29` · `7.146.38` · `7.161.20`

## Why this is a supply chain problem, not an application problem

Artifactory is an **artifact registry** — it is the thing every build system trusts by definition. Admin on the registry is not admin on one server; it is **write access to the binaries every downstream pipeline pulls without re-verification**. The blast radius is the set of everything built after the compromise, not the host.

The **disclosure-to-exploitation gap was days**, and exploitability is default-configuration. The practical patch window here is shorter than a normal change cycle.

## A timeline coincidence worth resolving deliberately

`Guides/AI-BugBounty/openai-huggingface-agent-swarm-reward-hacking-artifactory-0day-2026.md` records that OpenAI's evaluation agents escaped the ExploitGym sandbox in **late June 2026** via a then-zero-day in a locally hosted, internet-connected **JFrog Artifactory** instance, which OpenAI says it disclosed to JFrog.

⚠️ **Whether CVE-2026-82329 is that same vulnerability is not established by any source read this sweep, and must not be assumed.** It is logged here so the question gets answered on purpose rather than asserted by coincidence. If it *is* the same bug, the notable fact is that an AI agent found it first.

## Action

1. **Patch to the listed fixed versions now.** This is a default-config, pre-auth admin bypass under active exploitation.
2. **Audit access tokens** — enumerate admin tokens and API keys created since disclosure and revoke anything not explicitly accounted for. The reported attack outcome is *token creation*, so patching alone leaves attacker access in place.
3. Review artifact upload/overwrite history for the same window; treat any unexplained publish as a supply chain incident affecting downstream consumers, not a registry hygiene issue.
4. Remove Artifactory from direct internet exposure.

## Open questions

- Exploitation attribution and IOCs not published in the sources read.
- Whether observed exploitation is opportunistic scanning or targeted is unstated.
- Relationship (if any) to the June 2026 ExploitGym escape zero-day — unresolved.

## Sources

> Source: [The Hacker News — Attackers Exploit Critical JFrog Artifactory Flaw to Mint Admin Tokens Days After Disclosure](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-critical-jfrog.html) — 2026-09-01
> Source: [CCCS — JFrog security advisory (AV26-867)](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/jfrog-security-advisory-av26-867) — 2026-09-01

## Tags

#cve-2026-82329 #jfrog #artifactory #authentication-bypass #supply-chain #exploited-in-the-wild #watchtowr #cccs

---

## Update — 2026-09-03: exploitation corroborated by watchTowr and CCCS

**watchTowr reports in-the-wild exploitation** of CVE-2026-82329 (CVSS 9.8), and the **Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issued AV26-867 Update 1** on 2026-09-02 acknowledging open-source reporting of exploitation.

**Affected versions (per CCCS):** multiple JFrog Artifactory branches prior to **7.111.21 through 7.161.20** — check the specific branch you run rather than assuming a single fixed version.

**Timeline detail worth recording:** exploitation is reported as beginning **days after disclosure**. That is the compressed window this vault has now seen repeatedly for internet-facing enterprise software, and it is the operational argument against treating a 9.8 in a build system as a normal patch-cycle item.

**Why the Artifactory case is worse than a generic auth bypass.** An artifact repository is a **supply-chain root of trust**. Administrative access does not merely expose the repository — it permits **replacing or republishing binaries that every downstream build consumes**, and those binaries are then distributed by the victim's own trusted pipeline. The correct incident scope for a compromised Artifactory is therefore not the server; it is **every artifact published or served since the compromise window opened**, and every environment that consumed them.

This sweep separately logged the **Virtualizor BGP-hijack** malicious-update case. Read together, the pattern is consistent: **attackers are targeting the distribution layer rather than the endpoint**, because one compromise there is worth thousands downstream.

**Additional action:**

1. Upgrade to the fixed build **for your branch** (7.111.21+ / … / 7.161.20+ as applicable).
2. **Audit all admin tokens and access tokens**, not just user accounts — the flaw mints tokens, so revoking a user does not revoke the attacker's access. Revoke and reissue.
3. Compare artifact checksums against known-good build outputs for the exposure window.
4. Review Artifactory audit logs for token creation events and for pulls/pushes from unexpected principals.

> Source: [The Hacker News — Attackers Exploit Critical JFrog Artifactory Flaw to Mint Admin Tokens Days After Disclosure](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-critical-jfrog.html) — 2026-09-01
> Source: [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security — JFrog security advisory (AV26-867) Update 1](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/jfrog-security-advisory-av26-867) — 2026-09-02

CVE-2026-83548.body:
# SonicWall SMA1000 — CVE-2026-83549 & CVE-2026-83548 (Second Zero-Day Chain, Exploited in the Wild)

⚠️ **Verification:** Multiple outlets relaying a single underlying document — SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer both reporting SonicWall's own advisory. Not independent confirmation.

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical | **Date logged:** 2026-09-02
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-83549, CVE-2026-83548
**Status:** **Exploited in the wild** (vendor statement)
**Product:** SonicWall SMA1000 appliances

## Summary

SonicWall has warned of **two SMA1000 zero-days actively exploited in the wild**: **CVE-2026-83549** and **CVE-2026-83548**. Chained, they yield **unauthenticated remote code execution** on the appliance.

## Why this is a separate note

This vault already tracks a **different** SMA1000 zero-day chain from July 2026 — `CVE-2026-15409` (SSRF, CVSS 10.0) and `CVE-2026-15410` (post-auth command injection) — in `Threat_Intel/CVEs/2026/Critical/SonicWall-SMA1000-CVE-2026-15409-15410-ZeroDay-Exploited.md`.

**This is the second exploited pre-auth RCE chain in the same product line inside roughly ten weeks.** The pattern, not the individual CVE, is the finding: SMA1000 is behaving as a standing liability rather than a patch-queue item — the same conclusion this vault reached about Langflow after its fourth unauthenticated-execution CVE.

## Document class

Two outlets, one underlying document. Both SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer are relaying **SonicWall's own advisory**; neither reports independent observation of exploitation. The vendor is a good source for the fact of exploitation and a poor source for its scale.

## Action

1. **Patch immediately** to the fixed SonicWall release.
2. If patching cannot be immediate, take the SMA1000 Work Place and management interfaces **off the public internet**.
3. Because exploitation is pre-auth and in the wild, **assume compromise on any internet-reachable appliance** — rotate appliance admin credentials, session tokens, and any VPN/SSO secrets the appliance holds.
4. Hunt for anomalous outbound connections from the appliance and unexpected management-console command history.
5. Diff the appliance configuration and interface inventory **out-of-band** against a known-good baseline — the Fire Ant lesson applies: implants can filter local `show` output but rarely remove the structure they depend on.

## Open questions

- **CVSS scores, affected version ranges and fixed builds were not captured in the read** — pull directly from the SonicWall PSIRT advisory before acting on version numbers.
- No IOCs published in either source.
- **Whether these are a bypass of the July `CVE-2026-15409` / `CVE-2026-15410` fixes is unknown and worth resolving** — a patch bypass would change the response.

## Sources

> Source: [SecurityWeek — SonicWall Warns of Two SMA1000 Zero-Days Exploited in Attacks](https://www.securityweek.com/sonicwall-warns-of-two-sma1000-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/) — 2026-09-02
> Source: [BleepingComputer — SonicWall SMA1000 zero-days](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/) — 2026-09-02

## Tags

#cve-2026-83549 #cve-2026-83548 #sonicwall #sma1000 #zero-day #exploited-in-the-wild #edge-device #unauthenticated-rce

---

## Update — 2026-09-03: added to CISA KEV; CVSS 10.0 confirmed for CVE-2026-83548

**CISA added seven actively exploited flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-09-03, including CVE-2026-83548**, now reported with **CVSS 10.0** and characterised as a **pre-authentication SSRF** in SonicWall SMA 1000.

Two of the open questions from the original note are now partly answered:

- **CVSS: CVE-2026-83548 = 10.0.** The vulnerability class is **SSRF**, not (as might have been assumed) a memory-safety bug.
- **The exploitation claim is no longer vendor-only.** CISA KEV addition is an independent government assertion of in-the-wild exploitation, which upgrades the document class from "vendor advisory relayed by two outlets" to corroborated. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security also issued **AV26-872 Update 1** on 2026-09-02 naming both CVEs as exploited and advising immediate update, affecting **SMA1000 6210 / 7210 / 8200v**.

**The SSRF detail sharpens the July comparison and is worth dwelling on.** The July 2026 chain in this same product line was `CVE-2026-15409` — **also an SSRF, also CVSS 10.0** — chained with a post-auth command injection. **That is now two CVSS-10.0 pre-auth SSRF-rooted RCE chains in SMA1000 inside roughly ten weeks.** The recurrence of the same root cause class strongly suggests an architectural pattern (an internal service reachable via request forgery from the unauthenticated surface) rather than two independent coding errors, and it raises the specific question the original note flagged: **whether CVE-2026-83548 is a bypass of the CVE-2026-15409 fix.** That question is now materially more likely to be answered "yes" and should be resolved with the vendor.

**Revised action:** the original note recommended patching immediately and assuming compromise on internet-reachable appliances. That stands, but the KEV addition means **US federal agencies now have a binding remediation deadline**, and the pattern evidence supports a stronger recommendation: treat SMA1000 as a product line requiring **compensating controls independent of patching** — source-IP restriction or an authenticating proxy in front of the appliance — because a third chain within the quarter is now a reasonable planning assumption.

**Affected models (per CCCS AV26-872 U1):** SMA1000 6210, 7210, 8200v.

> Source: [The Hacker News — CISA Adds Seven Exploited Flaws as Attackers Deploy Reverse Shells and Crypto Miners](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/cisa-adds-seven-exploited-flaws-as.html) — 2026-09-03

# CVE-2026-85046 — Chrome V8 Type Confusion Zero-Day, Actively Exploited in the Wild

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical | **Date logged:** 2026-09-04
**Product:** Google Chrome — V8 JavaScript/WebAssembly engine
**Fixed in:** Chrome **152.0.7977.82 / .83** (emergency out-of-band release)
**Impact:** Arbitrary code execution inside the browser renderer sandbox via a crafted HTML page
**Status:** **Actively exploited in the wild** — Google confirmed an exploit exists; targets and actor undisclosed

## Summary

Google shipped an **emergency Chrome update** for **CVE-2026-85046**, a **type confusion** flaw in **V8**, the JavaScript and WebAssembly engine Chrome uses to process web content. A crafted HTML page achieves **arbitrary code execution inside the renderer sandbox**. Google confirmed **real-world exploitation** but, per its standard practice, withheld attack details, targeting, and actor attribution until a majority of users have updated.

## Reading the sandbox qualifier honestly

The "inside the sandbox" framing consistently causes under-prioritisation, and it should not here.

- **A renderer-only bug is still full access to everything the tab holds** — session cookies, tokens in memory, the DOM of every same-process origin, and the credential autofill surface. For a browser that is now the primary enterprise application client, that is the crown-jewel boundary, not a stepping stone to it.
- **Renderer RCE is the standard first stage of a chain.** Every in-the-wild Chrome chain this vault has logged pairs a V8 or WebAssembly bug with a separate sandbox-escape primitive. The absence of a disclosed escape means the escape was not disclosed, not that the operator lacks one.
- **V8 type confusion is the single most productive Chrome bug class** and the one with the shortest interval from patch to public n-day exploit, because the patch diff points directly at the affected optimisation path. Assume a working public exploit within days of this note.

## Relationship to the 2026-09-02 browser patch cycle

This is **not** the same event as `Threat_Intel/Browser-Patch-Cycle-Chrome-Firefox-2026-09-02.md`. That note covered a scheduled Chrome/Firefox round with **no reported exploitation**, and explicitly recorded that Chrome fixed versions had not been captured. This is an **out-of-band emergency release two days later with confirmed exploitation**. An estate that treated the 09-02 cycle as routine and deferred it is now two patch levels behind on an actively exploited engine bug.

## Action

1. **Force Chrome to 152.0.7977.82/.83 or later now.** Chrome updates on relaunch — pushing the binary is not the same as applying it. **Measure relaunch compliance, not download compliance**; the gap between the two is where this bug lives.
2. Update every **Chromium derivative**: Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Electron applications, and embedded CEF/WebView2 components. Electron apps are the reliably forgotten surface and ship their own pinned Chromium.
3. Enforce a **maximum browser version age** policy via management (Chrome Enterprise / Intune) rather than relying on user relaunch.
4. **Hunt:** renderer process crashes (`chrome.exe` / `Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)`) clustered by user or by site, unexpected child processes spawned from a renderer, and outbound connections from browser processes to newly-seen domains.
5. Treat as **in-scope for KEV-style SLA** — confirmed exploitation on a universally deployed client.

## Open questions

- **Whether a sandbox escape was chained.** Google has not said. This is the question that determines whether the impact is tab-scoped or host-scoped.
- Targeting: no indication yet whether this is commercial-surveillance, state-aligned, or criminal use.
- No IOCs published.
- Whether the bug affects Chrome for Android and iOS builds on the same timeline.

## Sources

> Source: [@TheHackersNews](https://x.com/TheHackersNews/status/2095773697412079741) — 2026-09-04 07:19 UTC — "Attackers are exploiting a Chrome V8 zero-day. CVE-2026-85046 allows arbitrary code execution inside the browser sandbox via a crafted HTML page. Google fixed it in Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83."
> Source: [@The_Cyber_News](https://x.com/The_Cyber_News/status/2095767967577600011) — 2026-09-04 06:56 UTC — emergency Chrome security update for a critical zero-day already exploited in real-world attacks.

# CVE-2026-9586 — Sangoma Switchvox Unauthenticated SQL Injection to RCE (Exploited in the Wild)

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** Critical (CVSS 9.3) | **Date logged:** 2026-09-03
**Product:** Sangoma Switchvox (SMB Edition 8.3) VoIP platform
**Impact:** Unauthenticated SQL injection leading to remote code execution
**Status:** **Actively exploited** — attackers deploying reverse shells

## Summary

**CVE-2026-9586** is an **unauthenticated SQL injection** in the Sangoma Switchvox VoIP platform that leads to **remote code execution**. Attackers are exploiting it in the wild to **deploy reverse shells**.

## Why a PBX compromise is worse than its CVSS suggests

A phone system is not a peripheral. A compromised PBX gives an attacker:

- **A trusted internal network position.** VoIP servers are routinely placed with broad internal reachability and are almost never segmented as tightly as their access warrants.
- **Call metadata and often call recordings** — who spoke to whom, when, for how long. That is a targeting dataset for social engineering and, for legal, HR or executive functions, a confidentiality incident on its own.
- **Outbound calling under the organisation's own caller ID.** Vishing from the victim's real number defeats the primary verification heuristic staff are taught. This sweep also carries Unit 42's *Spring Ring* Teams-vishing research; a compromised PBX is a materially better position than a spoofed one.
- **Toll fraud**, the classic and immediate monetisation.

## Action

1. **Patch Switchvox immediately.** Exploitation is unauthenticated and active.
2. **Remove the Switchvox admin and web interfaces from internet exposure.** Unauthenticated pre-auth RCE on an internet-facing appliance means exposure equals compromise.
3. **Assume compromise on any internet-reachable instance.** Hunt for reverse-shell processes, unexpected outbound connections from the PBX, new admin users and modified dialplan/extension configuration.
4. Review call-detail records for anomalous outbound volume and destinations (toll fraud is the fastest confirmation signal).
5. Rotate SIP trunk credentials and any directory/LDAP bind accounts the PBX holds.
6. **Segment the PBX.** It should not be able to reach general server VLANs.

## Open questions

- Exact affected/fixed version ranges beyond "SMB Edition 8.3" not captured — pull from the Sangoma advisory.
- No IOCs published in the read.
- Whether the flaw is in a specific endpoint or broadly reachable is unstated.

# Five Critical WordPress Plugin & Theme Flaws — Site Takeover / RCE (2026-08-29)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

## The five

| CVE | CVSS | Product | Primitive | Affected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-76581 | 9.8 | **WPMU DEV Dashboard** plugin | Authentication bypass → administrator | ≤ 5.0.1 |
| CVE-2026-18431 | 9.8 | **Avada** theme | Arbitrary file write → PHP write → RCE | ≤ 7.16 (with Fusion Builder ≤ 3.16) |
| CVE-2026-19632 | 9.8 | **TranslatePress** | Sensitive info exposure → admin password-reset URL | ≤ 3.3.1 |
| CVE-2026-19598 | 9.8 | **Pods** | Unauth privilege escalation / password overwrite | ≤ 3.3.9 |
| CVE-2026-82222 | **10.0** | **GiveWP** | PHP object injection → OS command execution | ≤ 4.16.7.1 |

Already tracked separately: [[CVE-2026-19598-WordPress-Pods-Unauth-Privilege-Escalation-ForceUpdate]], [[CVE-2026-82222-GiveWP-WordPress-Unauth-RCE]].

## Preconditions are the whole story on three of these

The severity numbers are uniform (9.8/10.0); the *reachability* is not. Read the conditions, not the score:

- **WPMU DEV Dashboard (CVE-2026-76581)** — only on sites **connected to WPMU DEV with Hub SSO enabled and mapped to an administrator**. Narrow, but where it applies it is unauthenticated-to-admin in one step.
- **Avada (CVE-2026-18431)** — requires the **Fusion Builder plugin installed and active**. Avada ships with Fusion Builder as its page builder, so in practice this is close to "all Avada sites". The theme-plus-bundled-plugin pairing means the vulnerable condition is the **shipped default**, not an opt-in.
- **TranslatePress (CVE-2026-19632)** — requires **automatic string saving enabled** *and* the target administrator's **profile locale set to a published secondary language**. Genuinely conditional. But note what leaks: not a hash, the **plaintext reset key and login parameters** — i.e. a working account-takeover primitive, not a credential to crack.

## GiveWP root cause — this supersedes the earlier reading

Patchstack's own description of CVE-2026-82222:

> The flaw chains a broken "safe unserialize" helper, a donation flow that feeds that helper attacker-controlled data, and a gadget chain in code that GiveWP ships.

And their generalisation:

> …how PHP object injection turns into remote code execution when three ingredients line up: a place to store an attacker-controlled serialized object, code that later unserializes it, and a gadget chain in loaded classes.

The stated preconditions are **one published donation form and one active payment gateway** — which is the definition of a functioning donation site. See the correction logged in [[CVE-2026-82222-GiveWP-WordPress-Unauth-RCE]].

## The pattern worth keeping

Three of the five are **authorization or trust logic that fails open**, not memory safety:

- WPMU DEV: an SSO mapping trusted without verifying who asserted it.
- Pods: an error path that returns before enforcing capability, nonce and login checks.
- GiveWP: a sanitiser trusted to strip objects that does not, plus data read back from the **database treated as trusted** because it came from "inside".

That last one is the transferable finding. **Round-tripping attacker data through your own database does not launder it.** Anywhere an application serialises user input, stores it, and later unserialises it on read, the storage layer is doing nothing but delaying the injection.

## Action

1. Inventory: Avada + Fusion Builder, WPMU DEV Dashboard, TranslatePress, Pods, GiveWP. Patch all past the affected ranges.
2. **Avada is the priority for most estates** — commercial theme, very large install base, vulnerable in its default configuration, and the primitive is unauthenticated file write to RCE.
3. TranslatePress mitigations short of patching: disable automatic string saving, or set administrator profile locales to the primary language.
4. Post-patch hunt: unexpected administrator accounts, password changes on privileged users, new PHP files under `wp-content/uploads`, and PHP worker processes spawning shells.

> Source: [The Hacker News — Five Critical WordPress Plugin and Theme Flaws Enable Site Takeover or RCE](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/five-critical-wordpress-plugin-and.html) — Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:25 UTC

# CISA KEV Additions, 26 August 2026 — Six Exploited Flaws (Citrix NetScaler, Linux Kernel, MS SQL Server, Red Hat ABRT, AjaxPro)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Date added:** 2026-08-26
**FCEB deadline:** BleepingComputer reports CISA ordered federal agencies to patch the **Citrix NetScaler** flaw **by Saturday** (2026-08-29) — a ~3-day window.

## The six

| CVE | Product | Class |
|---|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-8452** | **Citrix NetScaler ADC / Gateway** | Improper restriction of operations within buffer bounds → DoS |
| CVE-2019-1068 | Microsoft **SQL Server** | RCE in the context of the SQL Server Database Engine service account |
| CVE-2022-0995 | **Linux Kernel** | Out-of-bounds write → local privilege escalation / DoS |
| CVE-2015-5287 | Red Hat **ABRT** | Privilege escalation |
| CVE-2015-3246 | (libuser / related) | Unauthenticated local user corrupts `/etc/passwd` → DoS or privilege escalation |
| CVE-2021-23758 | **Ajax.NET Professional (AjaxPro)** | Deserialization of untrusted data → RCE via arbitrary .NET classes |

## Active exploitation of CVE-2026-8452
**Previdian** and **Defused Cyber** both report ongoing exploitation:
- Attackers dropping web shells named **`x.php`** and **`z.php`**
- Running discovery commands: **`id`**, **`echo`**
- **36 exploitation attempts in 12 days from 12 unique attacker IPs**, sourced from **Switzerland, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Netherlands, Russia, Singapore, Türkiye, USA, Vietnam**

⚠️ **Note the mismatch:** the CVE is classed as a **denial-of-service** issue, but the observed post-exploitation is **web shell deployment and command execution**. Either the DoS classification understates the primitive, or the web shells arrive via a chained second flaw. Recorded as an open discrepancy — **do not treat CVE-2026-8452 as "only a DoS" on the strength of the catalog text.** This is the third instance in recent sweeps of the published description being narrower than observed behaviour.

## The old-CVE cluster
Four of the six are from **2015, 2019, 2021 and 2022**. Their addition follows a **Cisco Talos** report on a Chinese cybercrime group. Old, unglamorous Linux and .NET privilege-escalation bugs are being actively used because the affected estate is long-lived: appliances, build servers, and legacy web apps that nobody re-images.

## Action
1. **Citrix NetScaler ADC / Gateway: patch now.** Hunt for `x.php` and `z.php` in web roots regardless of patch status.
2. Sweep Linux hosts for CVE-2022-0995 and CVE-2015-5287 exposure — especially appliances and long-uptime servers.
3. Inventory for **AjaxPro** — an easy one to miss; it is a decade-old .NET AJAX library still embedded in line-of-business apps.
4. Confirm SQL Server 2019-era patching on any instance whose service account is not minimally privileged.

## Related
CISA added **three further KEV entries on 27 August 2026** (see CISA advisory feed) — a second addition within 24 hours.

# CVE-2026-0251 — Palo Alto GlobalProtect App: Local Privilege Escalation + AD Password Recovery

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Type:** Local privilege escalation / credential exposure | **CVSS 3.1:** 7.8 (High) | **Date:** 2026-08-25

## Summary
Security researcher **Martijn van Ramesdonk** publicly disclosed **five high-risk vulnerabilities** in the **Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect** VPN and endpoint agent, originally reported to the vendor in **early April 2026**. **Two** of the five were folded into **CVE-2026-0251** (untrusted search path / local privilege escalation).

## Impact
- A **local, low-privileged user** can escalate to **`NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`** on Windows and to **root** on macOS and Linux.
- Turns any endpoint foothold into full administrative control — a post-exploitation accelerator, not an initial-access bug.
- Separately, the researcher demonstrated **recovery of the user's Active Directory password directly from the endpoint** by abusing privileged GlobalProtect components. This is the more consequential finding: it converts a local compromise into **domain-credential theft** without touching a DC.

## Affected
GlobalProtect App across **Windows, macOS and Linux**. Consult the vendor advisory for exact fixed builds — Palo Alto has patched the two CVE-2026-0251 issues.

## Disclosure friction (researcher's account — single source)
- The two CVE-2026-0251 bugs were **patched silently**, with **no notification to the reporter and no credit in the advisory**, which prompted the researcher to go public.
- **Two further vulnerabilities were ruled out of scope** for the bug bounty programme.
- A **fifth remains unpatched and undisclosed** while remediation continues.

**Read with care:** the technical findings are corroborated by the vendor advisory and NVD. The narrative about notification, credit and scope decisions comes from the researcher only; Palo Alto has not published a counter-account. Record it as a disclosure-process claim, not established fact.

## Action
- Inventory GlobalProtect App versions across all endpoints (not just the gateways — this is the **client-side** agent).
- Patch to the fixed build identified in the vendor advisory for CVE-2026-0251.
- Treat the AD-password-recovery technique as **live and unmitigated by patching alone** until Palo Alto confirms which component was hardened. Endpoints where a low-privileged compromise has occurred should have the associated AD credentials rotated.
- One flaw is **still unpatched** — this note is not closed.

## Distinguish from
This is **not** [[PaloAlto-GlobalProtect-Exploitation-2026]] (CVE-2026-0257, PAN-OS/Prisma Access **unauthenticated auth bypass**, actively exploited since May 2026). Same product family, different attack surface: that one is remote and pre-auth on the gateway; this one is local and post-auth on the client.

> Sources: [Palo Alto Networks Security Advisory CVE-2026-0251](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-0251); [Cyber Security News](https://cybersecuritynews.com/5-vulnerabilities-palo-alto-globalprotect/) — Tue, 25 Aug 2026 04:29 UTC; [GBHackers](https://gbhackers.com/5-palo-alto-globalprotect-flaws/); [@The_Cyber_News](https://x.com/The_Cyber_News/status/2092107019465728394) — 25 Aug 2026

# CVE-2026-0273 — Palo Alto PAN-OS Command Injection (Root)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** High
**Product:** Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS
**Type:** Command injection → arbitrary command execution as root
**Status:** Patched (Palo Alto advisory)

## Summary
Palo Alto Networks fixed a command injection vulnerability in PAN-OS, tracked as CVE-2026-0273, that allows an attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands as the **root** user. PAN-OS powers Palo Alto firewalls and is a frequent target for nation-state and ransomware actors given its network-edge position.

## Remediation
- Apply the fixed PAN-OS release per Palo Alto Networks' security advisory.
- Restrict management-plane access (no internet-exposed mgmt interface); use jump hosts / allowlists.

# CVE-2026-19912 / CVE-2026-19913 — Kaltura mwEmbed (html5lib): Unauthenticated Deserialization → Arbitrary File Read + RCE — **NO PATCH**

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** High → Critical in effect (unauthenticated RCE)
**Component:** Kaltura **mwEmbed** HTML5 video player library, also distributed as **html5lib**
**Endpoint:** `mwEmbedLoader.php`
**Patch status:** ❌ **None.** CERT/CC states it was **"unable to reach Kaltura to coordinate these vulnerabilities."**
**Exploitation:** None reported at time of writing; neither CVE is in CISA KEV.

## Mechanism
Both CVEs stem from the **same unsafe deserialization** in the `mwEmbedLoader.php` endpoint. Neither requires authentication **nor a Kaltura session token**. Per CERT/CC, **network access to the endpoint is the only precondition**.

- **Arbitrary file read** from the server
- **Code execution** on the server

## Why this one is worse than its CVSS suggests
1. **No vendor contact.** CERT/CC could not reach Kaltura. There is no patch, no timeline, and no reason to expect one soon.
2. **Embedded library.** mwEmbed/html5lib ships inside other products and inside institutional video platforms — universities, LMS deployments, media portals. Many operators do not know they run it.
3. **No session token needed.** Most Kaltura hardening guidance assumes the API is protected by session tokens. This endpoint is not.

## Mitigation (CERT/CC guidance — this is all there is)
- **Restrict or disable external access** to `mwEmbedLoader.php`.
- Enforce a **strict allow-list for the `ServiceUrl` parameter**, permitting only legitimate backend API URLs.

## Hunting
```
# Web logs — any external hit is worth review while unpatched
grep -i "mwEmbedLoader.php" access.log
# Serialized-object markers in ServiceUrl / query params
grep -Ei "mwEmbedLoader.*(O:[0-9]+:|a:[0-9]+:\{)" access.log
```
Look for PHP serialized-object markers (`O:<len>:"ClassName"`, `a:<n>:{`) in any parameter reaching the endpoint.

## Action
1. Inventory for mwEmbed / html5lib — including inside third-party products and appliance images.
2. Block external access at the reverse proxy / WAF now; this is the only real control available.
3. Add to the third-party-risk register as **known-vulnerable, vendor-unresponsive**.
4. Re-check for a Kaltura advisory on each sweep.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/unpatched-kaltura-mwembed-flaws-could.html) — 2026-08-26

# CVE-2026-29509 — Das U-Boot NFS `nfs_readlink_reply()` Buffer Overflow

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** High (buffer overflow; requires malicious/compromised NFS server or MITM)
**Component:** Das U-Boot ≤ 2026.04-rc3 — `nfs_readlink_reply()` in `net/nfs-common.c`, when `CONFIG_CMD_NFS` is enabled
**Impact:** A malicious NFS server response can overflow a buffer during `readlink` handling, potentially corrupting memory / hijacking execution in the bootloader.

## Details
When `CONFIG_CMD_NFS` is enabled, U-Boot's `nfs_readlink_reply()` fails to bound the symlink data returned by the NFS server, allowing a buffer overflow. An attacker controlling the NFS server (or on-path) during a network boot can trigger the overflow. Affects boot-time trust, relevant to embedded/IoT devices that netboot over NFS.

## Action
- Update U-Boot past 2026.04-rc3 once patched; disable `CONFIG_CMD_NFS` if NFS boot is not required.
- Avoid NFS network boot over untrusted networks; pin/authenticate boot sources.

> Source: [X @CVEnew](https://x.com/CVEnew) — 2026-07-08 (cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-29509)

# CVE-2026-4342 — ingress-nginx Comment-Based Configuration Injection

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Date**: 2026-04-08
**Tags**: #cve #kubernetes #ingress-nginx #rce #config-injection #high
**Source**: X (@kubernetesio) — [https://x.com/kubernetesio/status/2041698295647453575](https://x.com/kubernetesio/status/2041698295647453575)
**CVE**: CVE-2026-4342
**Severity**: High
**Component**: ingress-nginx (Kubernetes ingress controller)

---

## Summary

A **high-severity** vulnerability in ingress-nginx allows an attacker to inject arbitrary nginx configuration directives via **comment-based injection** in ingress annotations or controller inputs. This can lead to nginx configuration corruption, ACL bypass, or potentially remote code execution depending on the injected directives.

---

## Affected Component

- **Project**: kubernetes/ingress-nginx
- **Version(s)**: See [GitHub issue #137893](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/137893) for affected range
- **Attack Surface**: Kubernetes cluster with ingress-nginx installed; attacker needs ability to create/modify Ingress resources

---

## Vulnerability Details

The flaw is a **comment-based nginx configuration injection** — specially crafted input containing nginx comment syntax can break out of the expected configuration context and inject malicious directives into the final nginx.conf file generated by the ingress controller.

**Attack Scenario:**
1. Attacker has namespace-level permissions to create Ingress objects (common in multi-tenant clusters)
2. Crafts an annotation or field value containing nginx comment escape
3. Injected nginx directive lands in the generated config
4. nginx reloads, activating the injected configuration
5. Impact: bypass upstreams, redirect traffic, expose internal services, or RCE

---

## Remediation

- Apply the patch referenced in [GitHub issue #137893](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/137893)
- Review RBAC — restrict who can create/modify Ingress resources
- Monitor ingress-nginx admission webhook logs for suspicious annotation values
- Use OPA/Kyverno policies to block unusual annotation characters

---

## References

- GitHub issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/issues/137893
- X thread: https://x.com/kubernetesio/status/2041698295647453575
- 840 likes / 166 reposts — widely flagged by the Kubernetes security community

# CVE-2026-43503 — "DirtyClone" Linux Kernel Local Privilege Escalation

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Class:** Local privilege escalation to **root** via in-memory rewrite of `/usr/bin/su`.
**Technique:** A local user rewrites the **cached (in-memory) copy** of `/usr/bin/su`; the on-disk binary is **never modified**, so file-integrity / audit checks (AIDE, Tripwire, IMA) come back **clean** while a root shell is granted.
**Context:** Reported as the **4th bug with this same failure mode in two months** — an emerging Linux kernel page-cache / mapping integrity bug class. Closely related to [[CVE-2026-46331-Linux-Cached-su-Poisoning-Root]].

## Detection / Mitigation
- File-integrity monitoring is **insufficient** (disk binary unchanged). Hunt for unexpected `su`/setuid execution, anomalous memory mappings of setuid binaries, and child processes of non-privileged shells spawning root.
- Apply kernel updates as they land; consider `kernel.yama`, reduced setuid surface, and exec/mmap telemetry (eBPF/Falco).

> Source: X @TheHackersNews (tweet 2070503122691367089) — 2026-06-26; 2nd source X @The_Cyber_News (tweet 2070671911319925166) — 2026-06-27.

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Technique:** Poisons the **cached copy of `/bin/su` in memory**; the binary on disk stays untouched, so **file-integrity checks come back clean** while the attacker already holds a root shell.

# ShieldBreak — Microsoft Defender Patch Bypass PoC for CVE-2026-50656 "RoguePlanet" (SYSTEM)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Type:** CVE patch bypass / PoC | **Severity:** High (base CVE CVSS 7.8) | **Date:** 2026-08-12

## Summary
Researcher **Chaotic Eclipse** (aka *INFINITE NIGHTMARE*, *MSNightmare*, *Nightmare-Eclipse*) released a public PoC named **ShieldBreak** demonstrating a **patch bypass** for **CVE-2026-50656** ("**RoguePlanet**"), a Microsoft Defender for Windows local privilege escalation flaw patched in **July 2026**.

The PoC was published on GitHub **hours after August Patch Tuesday**, with the researcher claiming a **100% success rate** on fully patched systems and **SYSTEM** access.

## Action
- Do not assume the July patch closes RoguePlanet — treat Defender LPE as an open risk pending Microsoft confirmation.
- Monitor for Defender service tampering and unexpected SYSTEM token acquisition.
- Track for an out-of-band Microsoft advisory / revised CVE.

## Related
- Same researcher previously published **LegacyHive** (Windows User Profile Service hive-load EoP) — see `Threat_Intel/CVEs/2026/High/Windows-LegacyHive-UserProfileService-PrivEsc-ZeroDay-2026.md`, patched 2026-08-13.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/shieldbreak-zero-day-poc-claims.html) — Wed, 12 Aug 2026; [@IntCyberDigest](https://x.com/IntCyberDigest/status/2087538376006135880) — 2026-08-12

## Update — 2026-08-17: ShieldBreak assigned CVE-2026-69414; Microsoft confirms it's building a patch

✅ **Verification (this update):** Verified — Microsoft statement + Will Dormann confirmation via BleepingComputer

- On **Friday 2026-08-15**, three days after disclosure, **Microsoft confirmed it is working on a patch** and is now tracking ShieldBreak as **CVE-2026-69414** ("elevation of privilege in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine in Microsoft Defender"). No patch yet at time of writing.
- Microsoft has **not** acknowledged that Nightmare Eclipse found it, and disputes framing — it publicly warned of **legal action** against those causing "real harm" to customers, widely read as aimed at the researcher.
- **Independent confirmation:** vulnerability analyst **Will Dormann** confirmed the PoC works, with the caveat that **Microsoft Defender must be enabled** for the escalation to succeed.
- Researcher's claim: **100% success rate → SYSTEM** on fully patched **Windows 11 25H2 (+Canary)** and **Windows Server 2025**; Windows 10 not "supported" by the PoC but stated to be vulnerable.
- ShieldBreak was disclosed **without notice to Microsoft** as part of an ongoing dispute over disclosure/bounty practices.
- Nightmare Eclipse's broader Defender/BitLocker/Windows zero-day set — **LegacyHive, RoguePlanet, BlueHammer, RedSun, YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, UnDefend**. Fixed so far: YellowKey/GreenPlasma/MiniPlasma (June PT), RoguePlanet (July, now bypassed), LegacyHive (Aug-13). **BlueHammer, RedSun, UnDefend and ShieldBreak/CVE-2026-69414 remain unpatched zero-days.**

### Action (updated)

# CVE-2026-52924 — Linux Kernel SCTP Out-of-Bounds (Ubuntu 26.04), Public Exploit

⚠️ **Verification:** Single source — an X post from @cybermeowfia claiming a working exploit against Ubuntu 26.04. Exploit source published on GitHub. Not independently confirmed in this read; treat the working-exploit claim as unverified until the repository or a vendor advisory is reviewed.

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** High | **Date logged:** 2026-09-04
**Product:** Linux kernel — **SCTP** (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) subsystem
**Affected:** demonstrated against **Ubuntu 26.04**
**Timeline claimed:** introduced **October 2017**, fixed upstream **June 2026** — a **~9-year** dwell time in-tree
**Discovery:** attributed to the **NebuSec** automated security pipeline

## Summary

A public exploit was released for **CVE-2026-52924**, an **out-of-bounds** flaw in the Linux kernel's **SCTP** implementation, demonstrated against **Ubuntu 26.04**. The bug is claimed to have been **introduced in October 2017 and fixed upstream in June 2026**, and to have been **discovered and exploited by an automated pipeline** rather than by manual review.

## The two findings worth separating

**First, the boring one: SCTP is attack surface almost nobody accounts for.** SCTP is a transport protocol most estates never knowingly use — it appears in telecom signalling (SIGTRAN/Diameter), some clustering stacks, and essentially nowhere else. But the kernel module is present and, on many distributions, **auto-loadable on first use of the protocol family**. That is the recurring shape of Linux local-privilege-escalation surface: not code you run, but code the kernel will load *on demand* if an unprivileged process asks for it. `AF_SCTP`, `AF_PACKET`, DCCP, TIPC, and n_hdlc have all supplied the same lesson.

**Second, the one that actually matters: a pipeline found and weaponised a nine-year-old bug.** This is the third item in roughly a week where the expensive, specialist part of exploitation was automated away — alongside **Forescout using Claude to port a WAGO PLC exploit between models** (2026-09-03) and **Unit 42's autonomous-agent enterprise breach** (2026-09-03). The pattern is now consistent enough to state plainly:

> **Bug age is no longer a proxy for bug safety.** The defence for old, obscure, in-tree code was never that it was secure — it was that no human would spend weeks auditing an unfashionable subsystem for a low-value LPE. Automation removes exactly that economic filter, and it removes it across the entire tree at once, not one subsystem at a time.

The practical consequence for triage: **a 2017-introduced kernel bug in an unused protocol is now a normal finding, not an exotic one.** Backlogs sorted by "recently introduced" or "in code we actually use" are sorted on an assumption that no longer holds.

## Action

1. **Apply current kernel updates.** Upstream fixed this in June 2026; the exposure is estates running kernels older than their distribution's June 2026 rebase.
2. **Blacklist SCTP if you do not use it** — this is the cheap, durable control and it neutralises the entire subsystem, not just this CVE:
   - `install sctp /bin/true` in `/etc/modprobe.d/`
   - Verify with `lsmod | grep sctp` and confirm nothing loads it on demand.
3. Apply the same reasoning to the other historically productive auto-loadable modules (`dccp`, `tipc`, `rds`, `n_hdlc`) unless a documented requirement exists.
4. **Detection:** alert on unexpected kernel module loads, and on `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_SCTP)` from processes that have no business speaking SCTP.
5. Prioritise on **multi-tenant and shared-shell hosts** — CI runners, jump boxes, container hosts with permissive seccomp — where an unprivileged local foothold is the realistic precondition.

## Open questions

- **The exploit claim is unverified in this read.** The GitHub repository should be reviewed before this is recorded as a working public exploit.
- Which distributions and kernel versions are affected beyond Ubuntu 26.04.
- Whether the primitive is a local privilege escalation only, or remotely reachable where SCTP listeners are exposed. The read implies local.
- **What NebuSec is** and whether its pipeline output is being published broadly — that would materially change the expected volume of this class of finding.

## Sources

> Source: [@cybermeowfia](https://x.com/cybermeowfia/status/2095706087064527011) — 2026-09-04 02:50 UTC — "Today's exploit is for the latest Ubuntu 26.04, a 9-year-old OOB in SCTP: CVE-2026-52924. It was introduced in Oct 2017 and fixed upstream in Jun 2026. Discovered and exploited by the NebuSec security pipeline."

# CVE-2026-53399 — Linux Kernel nfsd Layout Setlease Use-After-Free

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Type:** CVE / Linux kernel (nfsd, pNFS layout)
**Severity:** High — Red Hat CVSSv3 **7.0** (⚠️ X source claimed 9.8; see note)
**CVE:** CVE-2026-53399
**Date captured:** 2026-07-27

## Summary
Use-after-free in the Linux kernel **nfsd** subsystem. `nfs4_alloc_stid()` publishes the new stid into `cl->cl_stateids` via `idr_alloc_cyclic()` under `cl_lock` before returning to `nfsd4_alloc_layout_stateid()`. `nfsd4_free_layout_stateid()` unconditionally inspects `ls->ls_fence_work` via `delayed_work_pending()` under `ls_lock`, but `INIT_DELAYED_WORK(&ls->ls_fence_work, …)` runs only after the `setlease` call — so on the **setlease-failure path** the destructor touches an uninitialized/freed `delayed_work`.

## Impact
- UAF affecting confidentiality, integrity, availability (crash / potential code execution) on NFS servers exporting pNFS layouts.
- Affected: Linux kernel up to 6.12.95 / 6.18.38 / 7.1.2 (fixed in point releases; distros backporting).

## Note on severity
X source (@SecAlertsCo) billed this as **CVSS 9.8, network, no-auth**. Red Hat's published advisory (2026-07-19) rates it **7.0**. Treat the 9.8 as unverified vendor-inflation; prioritise by exposure of NFS/pNFS layout servers.

## Action
- Patch nfsd/kernel to fixed point releases; restrict NFS server exposure to trusted networks.
- Hunt for nfsd crashes / oops referencing `nfsd4_free_layout_stateid`.

> Source: X [@SecAlertsCo](https://x.com/SecAlertsCo) — 2026-07-26; web-verified via NVD CVE-2026-53399, VulDB #380130, Red Hat (CVSS 7.0).

# CVE-2026-64561 — Zapscape: KVM/x86 Guest-to-Host Escape (Shadow MMU UAF)

**Type:** Use-after-free / VM escape | **Date:** 2026-08-06 (public disclosure)

## Summary
**Zapscape** (**CVE-2026-64561**) is a **use-after-free in the shadow-MMU emulation of KVM/x86**, in the recursive **zap path** run when shadow pages are reclaimed. A privileged (kernel-level) attacker inside an **L1 guest** with **nested virtualization** exposed can **escape KVM isolation** to the host.

# CVE-2026-64564 — Linux Kernel SCTP UAF "SCTPhantom" (Local Root + Container Escape)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** High (CVSS v4.0 8.5)
**Status:** Patched
**Date captured:** 2026-08-08

## Summary
**SCTPhantom** is a **use-after-free** in the Linux kernel's SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) **Dynamic Address Reconfiguration (ASCONF)** handling. A local attacker can escalate to **root**, and in certain configurations **escape a container** to reach the host. Found by **Tencent Zhuque Lab's Corvus AI** project.

## Technical Detail
- Root cause: an identity mix-up — the kernel checks a delete request against the packet's source address but acts on a path chosen using a different address inside the message, leading to UAF.
- Present since Linux **2.6.25 (Dec 2007)** — ~18 years old.

## Affected / Fixed
- Fixed in stable kernels **7.1.6, 6.18.42, 6.12.101, 6.6.148** (released 2026-08-03). Disclosed 2026-08-06.

## Remediation
- Patch to a fixed stable kernel.
- If patching is delayed, disable/blacklist the `sctp` module where not needed (`modprobe -r sctp`; blacklist) to remove the attack surface.

# CVE-2026-64600 — "RefluXFS" Linux Kernel XFS Local Privilege Escalation to Root

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Type:** CVE / Linux kernel (XFS filesystem) — Local Privilege Escalation
**Severity:** High (root LPE; ~16.4M systems estimated)
**CVE:** CVE-2026-64600
**Date captured:** 2026-07-27

## Summary
**RefluXFS** is a race condition in the Linux kernel **XFS copy-on-write (reflink) path**. When two concurrent `O_DIRECT` writes target the same reflinked file, the kernel can briefly drop the inode lock while waiting for transaction log space. A second writer completes its own remap and alters the original block's reference state; when the first writer resumes it trusts stale metadata and writes **directly to the original block** instead of a private copy. An unprivileged local attacker can overwrite protected on-disk files (e.g. `/etc/passwd`, SUID-root binaries) → **root**.

## Impact
- Local unprivileged → root; on-disk corruption persists across reboots, limited forensic evidence.
- Not memory-corruption/hardening-bypass dependent — abuses concurrent O_DIRECT writes on reflink-enabled XFS.
- Default-affected: RHEL 8/9/10 and derivatives, Fedora Server, Amazon Linux. Qualys estimates 16.4M+ systems.

## Timeline
- Fix merged to Linux tree **2026-07-16**; Qualys public disclosure **2026-07-22**; distros backporting.

## Action
- Patch kernel; prioritise multi-tenant / shell-access hosts with reflink-enabled XFS (`xfs_info | grep reflink`).
- Where patching lags, restrict local access and monitor for unexpected writes to SUID binaries / `/etc/passwd`.

> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/linux/new-refluxfs-linux-flaw-lets-attackers-gain-root-privileges/) — 2026-07-23; web-verified via [Qualys](https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2026/07/22/refluxfs-a-linux-kernel-local-privilege-escalation-to-root-in-xfs-cve-2026-64600).

# CVE-2026-64638 — WordPress Core Pre-Auth XSS → PHP RCE ("XSS2Shell")

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 4 independent sources

**Severity:** High (CVSS 8.9)
**Status:** Patched (WordPress 7.0.3)
**Date captured:** 2026-08-08

## Summary
A **pre-authentication reflected XSS** in WordPress Core's login screen (`wp-login.php`) that can be chained into **server-side PHP remote code execution**. Discovered by **pwn.ai** — notably using **open-weight LLMs** — and dubbed **XSS2Shell**.

## Technical Detail
- The bug lives in the failed-login error path. Submitting a non-existent username builds an error message via `wp_strip_all_tags`.
- Inserting a space between an opening angle bracket and a tag name (e.g. `< area`) causes PHP's `strip_tags()` parser to treat the payload as harmless text, letting script through.
- The resulting JavaScript executes in the visitor's browser with no further interaction on that page (pre-auth).
- **RCE chain:** requires a victim already logged in as Administrator plus explicit interaction with an attacker-controlled page → JS drives admin actions to write PHP to the server.

## Affected / Fixed
- Vulnerable code has shipped since **WordPress 4.7** — effectively every actively maintained install (~43% of the web).
- **Fix: WordPress 7.0.3**, backported through the 4.7 branch. Auto-update sites patch automatically.

## Remediation
- Update to 7.0.3 (or the backported patch) ASAP.
- Confirm auto-updates are enabled.

## AI angle
Found autonomously by pwn.ai using open-source models — another data point in AI-discovered CVEs (see Guides/AI-BugBounty).

# CVE-2026-65105 — NVIDIA NemoClaw: Drive-By DNS Rebinding → Persistent Local Model Poisoning

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Severity:** High (unauthenticated remote → persistent agent compromise)
**Component:** NVIDIA **NemoClaw** deployment wrapper (Ollama backend for OpenClaw agents)
**Fixed in:** **v0.0.35** — macOS and Linux only. **Windows / WSL remains unfixed.**

## Root cause
To let the **OpenShell sandbox container** reach the Ollama inference backend, NemoClaw binds Ollama to **`0.0.0.0:11434`**. This:
1. **Disables Ollama's built-in Host header validation**, and
2. Exposes the API **to the entire local network with no authentication**.

## Attack chain
1. Victim visits a single attacker-controlled webpage.
2. **DNS rebinding** lets that page reach `localhost:11434` as same-origin.
3. The page calls **`/api/create`** to **rewrite the model's chat template**, appending attacker text to **every system message**.
4. The poisoning **persists across sessions** and is **invisible to API consumers** — it lives in the model template, not in any prompt or config the user reads.

## Impact
NemoClaw agents typically hold **filesystem, shell, source-control and cloud-credential access**. A poisoned template can instruct the agent to:
- write vulnerabilities into code that **passes casual review**
- **stay silent** about security problems it finds
- **exfiltrate** files, API keys or conversation contents to an external endpoint

This is a **drive-by agent hijack**: no user interaction beyond loading a page, no credential theft, and no artefact in the places a developer would look.

## Action
- Upgrade NemoClaw to **≥ v0.0.35**; on **Windows/WSL treat as unpatched**.
- Never bind Ollama to `0.0.0.0` — bind to `127.0.0.1` or a dedicated container network.
- Add firewall rules blocking external access to **11434**.
- **Re-pull / re-create any local model whose template may have been modified** — patching does not un-poison an already-modified template.
- Audit `/api/create` usage and model template diffs.

## Bug-bounty relevance
`0.0.0.0`-bound local inference endpoints + DNS rebinding is a **reusable pattern**, not a NemoClaw-specific bug. Any local AI runtime that drops Host validation to serve a container is a candidate: enumerate local LLM ports (11434 Ollama, 8080/1234 LM Studio, 5000 text-generation-webui) from a hosted page and test rebinding.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/a-malicious-webpage-could-poison-your.html) — 2026-08-25
> Source: [Cyera Research — Drive-By Agent Hijacking](https://www.cyera.com/research/nemoclaw-one-website-visit-to-hijack-your-ai-agent) — 2026-08-25
> Source: [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/25/nvidia-nemoclaw-flaw-let-attackers-poison-the-model-behind-a-developers-ai-agent/) — 2026-08-25

# CVE-2026-67394 — Plesk Local Privilege Escalation to Root

⚠️ **Verification:** Single source — government advisory (CCCS AV26-866) relaying the WebPros/Plesk fix

**Type:** cve | **Severity:** High | **Date logged:** 2026-09-02
**CVE:** CVE-2026-67394
**Vendor:** WebPros (Plesk)
**Affected:** prior to 18.0.79.9 and prior to 18.0.80.5
**Exploitation:** None reported

## Summary

A vulnerability in **Plesk** allows **privilege escalation to root**. Fixed in 18.0.79.9 and 18.0.80.5.

## Why a control-panel privesc is worse than it sounds

Plesk runs on **multi-tenant hosting servers**, where the security model already assumes lower-privileged local accounts exist and are hostile — that is the product's normal operating condition, not an edge case. Root on that host is therefore not a single-server compromise; it is **tenant isolation collapse** across every site on the box, plus whatever DNS, mail and database credentials the panel stores.

The privesc class is usually deprioritised because 'the attacker already needs local access'. On shared hosting, **the attacker always has local access** — it is sold to them.

## Action

1. Update Plesk to **18.0.79.9** / **18.0.80.5** or later.
2. On shared hosting, treat unpatched exposure as **cross-tenant**: after patching, rotate panel, database and mail credentials rather than assuming containment.
3. Review for unexpected root-owned cron entries, SUID binaries and new local accounts.

## Open questions

- CVSS score, technical mechanism and exploitation status not given in the advisory read.

## Sources

> Source: [CCCS — WebPros security advisory (AV26-866)](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/webpros-security-advisory-av26-866) — 2026-09-01

# CVE-2026-68820 — Windows AFD.sys (WinSock) Privilege Escalation Zero-Day, Exploited by Lazarus (CVSS 7.0)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Type:** CVE / local privilege escalation, zero-day | **Severity:** High (CVSS 7.0) | **Date:** 2026-08-11 (Patch Tuesday)

## Summary
**CVE-2026-68820** is a privilege-escalation flaw in the **Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (`AFD.sys`)**, the core kernel driver handling network socket operations. An attacker with code already running on a machine escalates to **SYSTEM**.

It was the **only flaw under active attack** in the August 2026 Patch Tuesday, and has been **exploited by the North Korean Lazarus Group since early July 2026** — roughly five weeks before the patch.

## Campaign — Operation Dream Job
- **Actor:** Lazarus (DPRK).
- **Targets:** Defense, aerospace, and aviation organisations in **France, Germany, Brazil, and India**.
- **Lure:** Fake recruiter approaches (LinkedIn etc.) impersonating firms such as Lockheed Martin and Enveil; victim opens a malicious PDF or installs a **trojanized PDF viewer**.
- **Payload:** New backdoor tracked as **Troy**, granting remote access.
- **C2:** Built almost entirely on infrastructure Lazarus does not own — compromised **Roundcube webmail** installs and CMS platforms (many vulnerable to **CVE-2025-49113**) infected with **RelayShell**, a previously undocumented PHP webshell relaying commands/responses through simple text files.

## Patch Tuesday context
Microsoft's August 2026 release fixed **398–418 vulnerabilities** (THN reports 398; SANS ISC reports 418 with 62 critical), including **2 publicly disclosed zero-days** and critical **QUIC** and **DNS Server** RCE bugs. CVE-2026-68820 was the sole in-the-wild exploited flaw.

## Action
- Deploy August 2026 Patch Tuesday with priority on CVE-2026-68820.
- Hunt for the Troy backdoor, trojanized PDF viewers, and outbound C2 to Roundcube/CMS hosts.
- Patch or retire Roundcube installs vulnerable to CVE-2025-49113; hunt for RelayShell PHP webshells (text-file command relay pattern).

> Source: [Check Point Research](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/shattering-the-dream-when-a-job-offer-becomes-a-zero-day-attack/) — 2026-08-12; [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/lazarus-exploits-windows-zero-day-to.html) — Wed, 12 Aug 2026; [SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33236) — Tue, 11 Aug 2026

# CVE-2026-73570 — Zimbra Collaboration SNMP Command Injection, Unauthenticated RCE (Actively Exploited)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/attackers-exploit-zimbra-snmp-flaw-for.html) — 2026-08-20 | [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-zimbra-rce-flaw-now-actively-exploited-in-attacks/) 2026-08-20 | Primary: **CERT Polska** bulletin


**Type:** CVE / command injection → unauthenticated RCE | **Severity:** High (CVSS 8.9) | **Date:** 2026-08-20 (exploitation); patched July 2026

## Summary
**CVE-2026-73570 (CVSS 8.9)** — command injection in **Zimbra Collaboration (ZCS) before 10.1.20**, exploitable **when the optional `zimbra-snmp` package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled**.

Per NVD: improper sanitisation of untrusted input during **SNMP notification processing** lets an **unauthenticated attacker send specially crafted SMTP requests** resulting in **arbitrary OS command execution as the `zimbra` user**.

**CERT Polska** issued a bulletin this week warning of **active exploitation**.

## The Interesting Bit
The injection is reached over **SMTP** but processed by the **SNMP notification path** — a cross-protocol handoff. Mail arrives, notification logic processes attacker-controlled content, and shell metacharacters survive into a command. Anyone who scoped their exposure by asking "is SNMP exposed to the internet?" would have concluded they were safe. The reachable surface is **port 25**, which is exposed by definition on a mail server.

## Precondition (scoping)
Exploitable only if **`zimbra-snmp` is installed AND SNMP notifications are enabled**. This is optional and not universal — check before panicking, but check properly.

## CERT Polska IOC Guidance
Inspect **`/var/log/zimbra.log`** for suspicious **Zimbra service restarts**, and check for files created in the last 30 days in:
- `/opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/`
- `/opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/`
- `/tmp/`

Webshell drops into the Jetty webapps directories are the expected post-exploitation step.

## Action
- **Upgrade to ZCS 10.1.20 or later** (patch released July 2026 — this is exploitation of an *available* patch, not a zero-day).
- If immediate patching is not possible, **disable SNMP notifications** / remove the `zimbra-snmp` package to remove the precondition.
- Run the CERT Polska file-creation and restart checks above before assuming you are clean.
- Rotate any credentials or keys accessible to the `zimbra` user if indicators are found.

## Related
- `Zimbra-ZimReaper-ZeroDay-Russian-Espionage-2026.md` — Laundry Bear (CL-STA-1114 / TA488 / Void Blizzard) targeting Zimbra since at least July 2025 via CVE-2025-66376 stored XSS → ZimReaper.
- `Zimbra-Classic-WebClient-Stored-XSS-2026.md`

Zimbra remains a persistently targeted mail platform. Treat any ZCS instance as a high-priority patch target.

#cve #zimbra #command-injection #rce #exploited-in-the-wild #cert-polska #mail-server

## 2026-08-25 Update — KEV deadline reached; exploitation scale quantified

> Sources: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-orders-urgent-patching-of-actively-exploited-zimbra-flaw/) — Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:45 UTC; [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/197693/security/u-s-cisa-adds-zimbra-collaboration-suite-zcs-flaw-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html); SC Media; Dark Reading; CCCS AV26-816 Upd 1

- **CISA added CVE-2026-73570 to KEV on 21 Aug 2026** with an FCEB remediation deadline of **24 Aug 2026** — a **three-day** clock.
- **CERT Polska** confirmed active exploitation in the wild.
- **Shadowserver identified 270+ compromised Zimbra Collaboration Suite instances** while scanning for exploitation artifacts. This is the first hard number on impact.
- CVSS recorded as **8.9**; unauthenticated RCE via **command injection in the SNMP monitoring component**, exploitable **when SNMP notifications are enabled**.
- Patched in **Zimbra 10.1.20, released 20 July 2026** — a **month before** KEV listing.

### Read
The exposure window here is entirely **operator-side**. The fix shipped 20 July; exploitation and KEV listing followed in late August. Same shape as [[CVE-2026-21962-Oracle-WebLogic-Proxy-PlugIn-Unauth-Access-KEV-Exploited]] in this sweep — **patched flaws, delayed deployment, KEV as the forcing function.** Dark Reading's framing ("shrinking window to patch") is the correct read of both.

### Immediate check
If SNMP notifications are **disabled**, the instance is not exploitable via this path — that is the fastest triage question, and a valid compensating control where patching lags.

# CVE-2026-75149 — Marimo Notebook: MCP Server Entry Command Injection (Edit Mode)

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Severity:** High — **CVSS v4 8.7 / CVSS v3.1 8.8**
**Component:** Marimo Python notebook software
**Affected:** versions **< 0.23.15** · **Fixed in 0.23.15** · CVE published **2026-08-19**

## Details
An attacker crafts a marimo notebook containing a **malicious MCP (Model Context Protocol) server entry with an arbitrary command embedded in it**. When a victim opens that notebook **in edit mode**, marimo's **vulnerable configuration handler processes the MCP server entry and launches the attacker-supplied command as a local subprocess** — **before any notebook cell is executed**.

The key detail for defenders: the usual mental model is "notebooks are dangerous because running cells runs code." Here **merely opening the file in edit mode is enough**. Notebook-review workflows that assume "I'll look before I run" do not protect against this.

## Distinguish from CVE-2026-39987
Marimo has a **second, separate** 2026 vulnerability in circulation — **CVE-2026-39987**, a **pre-auth RCE** in the marimo OSS server, notable for going **from disclosure to in-the-wild exploitation in under 10 hours** (Sysdig). These are different bugs with different preconditions; do not merge them.

## Action
- Upgrade marimo to **≥ 0.23.15**.
- Treat **untrusted `.py` marimo notebooks as executables**, not documents.
- Inspect notebooks for MCP server entries **before opening in edit mode** (plain-text `grep` for `mcp` / `command` keys).
- Confirm CVE-2026-39987 is also remediated on any marimo server.

## Wider pattern
Third MCP-configuration-as-code-execution issue tracked in this vault this month. **A file format that can carry an MCP server definition is a file format that can carry a command.** Same class as malicious `.mcp.json` / IDE workspace-config execution.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/marimo-notebook-flaw-could-run-mcp.html) — 2026-08-25
> Source: [Sysdig — Marimo OSS RCE, disclosure to exploitation in under 10 hours](https://www.sysdig.com/blog/marimo-oss-python-notebook-rce-from-disclosure-to-exploitation-in-under-10-hours) — CVE-2026-39987 context

# Next.js — Two Critical Unauthenticated RCE Flaws: CVE-2026-75604 (Windows Path Traversal) + AVIF Image Parsing

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Severity:** Critical (vendor) — CVE-2026-75604 **CVSS 9.0**
**Fixed in:** **15.5.24** (Maintenance LTS) and **16.3.3** (Active LTS), published **2026-08-25**

## The two flaws
1. **CVE-2026-75604 — Windows path traversal → unauthenticated RCE.**
   Affects Next.js applications using **both the Pages Router and App Router without Cache Components**, **only when the server runs on a Windows filesystem**. **Linux and macOS deployments are not affected.**
   Vercel: *"There is no known workaround for affected windows-hosted applications. You should upgrade immediately if your server is hosted on Windows."*
2. **AVIF image parsing → unauthenticated RCE** via a specially crafted **AVIF** file.

## The OS-conditional exploitability is the interesting part
A path-traversal that is exploitable only on Windows is a **path-separator normalisation gap**: backslash handling that Windows treats as a separator and the sanitiser does not. This is the same class as the PortSwigger tag-name parser-differential work tracked on 2026-08-25 — a component treats a character as structural, an upstream filter treats it as data.

Practical consequence: **a security team that tested on Linux CI and deployed to Windows IIS/Node hosts will have a clean test result and a vulnerable production estate.**

## AVIF as an attack surface
AVIF decoders are comparatively new, complex (AV1 intra-frame), and increasingly reachable from unauthenticated upload or remote-image-optimisation paths. Any framework that fetches and re-encodes arbitrary remote images is exposing a decoder to attacker-chosen bytes. Worth enumerating: `next/image` remote patterns, allowed domains, and whether the optimiser is reachable without auth.

## Action
```bash
npm install next@15.5.24   # 15.5 line
npm install next@16.3.3    # 16.3 line
```
- Inventory Next.js deployments by **host OS**, not just version — Windows hosts are the urgent set and have **no workaround**.
- Restrict `next/image` remote patterns to an explicit allow-list.
- Review WAF/edge logs for traversal sequences and anomalous AVIF uploads against image-optimisation endpoints.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/nextjs-patches-critical-avif-and.html) — 2026-08-28

# CVE-2026-76639 / CVE-2026-76640 — Unitree G1 EDU Humanoid Robot: Two Independent Root RCE Chains, One Starting from Bluetooth Proximity

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 1 independent source

**Severity:** High → Critical in effect (root on a physically embodied machine)
**Target:** **Unitree G1 EDU** humanoid robot
**Fixed firmware:** ⚠️ **Not verified.** No accessible Unitree guidance names a fixed release. **G1 EDU owners currently have no confirmed remediation target for either CVE.**

## The two chains

### CVE-2026-76639 — network-adjacent
Path through **`chat_go`** and **`bashrunner`** to root RCE.

### CVE-2026-76640 — Bluetooth Low Energy
Begins from **BLE proximity** and reaches **root on the robot's Locomotion PC**.

The Locomotion PC is the component that drives the robot's actuators. Root there is not a data-confidentiality problem — it is **arbitrary control of a moving 1.3m machine**, from an attacker standing within Bluetooth range with no credentials and no network access.

## Vendor timeline
- **July 2026** — Unitree patched the **cloud account-to-robot ownership check**.
- As of the **27 August 2026** disclosure, the current cloud-assisted route requires **an account already bound to the target G1**, or the relevant key material already in hand. The July fix therefore closed the *remote-takeover-by-anyone* route but **not** the two chains disclosed here.

## Why this class matters
Humanoid and quadruped research platforms are shipping into universities, logistics pilots and defence labs faster than their firmware update channels are maturing. The pattern here — a permissive local shell helper (`bashrunner`) reachable from a chat/command surface, plus an unauthenticated BLE pairing/command path — is the same pattern seen across consumer IoT, but the **impact ceiling is physical injury rather than data loss**.

Compare the **Shark robot vacuum certificate → root RCE** note already in the vault (`Guides/Shark-Robot-Vacuum-Certificate-Root-RCE-IoT-2026.md`): identical shape, different mass.

## Action (owners)
- **Assume unpatched.** Treat the robot as a hostile-capable device on the network.
- Isolate on a dedicated VLAN with no route to corporate resources.
- **Disable BLE when not actively pairing** — CVE-2026-76640 needs only proximity.
- Restrict physical access to the operating area; BLE range is the attack perimeter.
- Press Unitree for a named fixed firmware build; record the answer here when obtained.

## Bug-bounty relevance
Robotics vendors are an under-tested surface with a growing installed base. Reusable checklist: BLE GATT characteristics accepting command strings; any helper binary named `*runner`/`*_exec` reachable from an IPC or chat surface; cloud ownership-binding checks that gate control but not local transports.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/two-unitree-g1-edu-humanoid-robot-flaws.html) — 2026-08-28

# CVE-2026-20262 — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Arbitrary File Write (Actively Exploited)

✅ **Verification:** Verified — 3 independent sources

**Severity:** Medium — CVSS 3.1 base **6.5** (vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N) — but **actively exploited** (CISA KEV, federal fix-by **2026-06-29**)
**Product:** Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage)
**Type:** Directory/path traversal → **arbitrary file write** by an authenticated low-privileged remote user; can chain to **root**
**Status:** Patched — update to a fixed release

## Summary
A flaw in the web interface of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager lets an **authenticated** remote attacker (valid low-privileged account) create or overwrite files on the underlying OS via a crafted HTTP request, due to improper validation of user-supplied input during file uploads. A successful write can be leveraged for **privilege escalation to root**. Cisco reports it has been **exploited in limited, targeted attacks**, and CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

## Exploitation indicators (from THN/Cisco)
Suspicious **WAR file uploads** to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Hunt in **`/var/log/nms/vmanage-server.log`** for path-traversal patterns such as:

```
../../../../var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/suspicious.war
```

A `.war` deployed into the WildFly `deployments` directory is a classic web-shell / RCE staging primitive.

## Defender actions
- **Update to a fixed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager release** immediately (KEV deadline 2026-06-29).
- Grep `vmanage-server.log` for `../` traversal sequences and unexpected `.war` deployments under `wildfly/standalone/deployments/`.
- Restrict and audit low-privileged web UI accounts; place the management interface behind VPN/allowlist.
- Review file integrity on the appliance and hunt for web shells / unexpected root processes.

## Sources

CVE-2026-68480.body:
# CVE-2026-68480 — Interrupt Injection ("TONTOU"): Spectre v2 Defense Bypass

⚠️ **Verification:** Unverified — 2 independent sources

**Type:** CPU speculative-execution side-channel | **Date:** 2026-08-06

## Summary
**MIT CSAIL** researchers **Daniël Trujillo & Mengjia Yan** disclosed **Interrupt Injection** (BleepingComputer: **"TONTOU"**), which **bypasses Spectre v2 mitigations** on **Intel and AMD** CPUs by exploiting a **Time-of-Neutralization → Time-of-Use** gap. An unprivileged program **times a hardware interrupt** to land between the CPU sanitizing its branch predictor and the kernel using it, **re-poisoning the predictor after the defense ran**.

## Impact
- **AMD Zen 2**, Linux 6.14 with all default Spectre v2 mitigations on: leaked **arbitrary kernel memory at 5.47 B/s, 91.97% accuracy** — enough to read **/etc/shadow** (password hashes) in **5 of 10** attempts.
- **No privileges** needed — only **local code execution**. Risk concentrated on **shared/multi-tenant** hosts.
- **Intel:** no end-to-end leak demonstrated (needs a usable in-kernel disclosure gadget).

## Patch
- Linux commit *"x86/bugs: Make Safe-RET robust against interrupt injection"* (AMD engineers, dated Jun 2). Fixed in stable **6.18.43, 6.6.149, 6.1.181** → **CVE-2026-68480**.

## Action
- Patch Linux kernels on shared/multi-tenant systems; prioritize AMD Zen 2 hosts running untrusted local workloads.

> Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/new-interrupt-injection-attack-can.html) — 2026-08-06 (RSS: THN feedburner)
> Source: [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-tontou-cpu-attack-bypasses-spectre-v2-fixes-leaks-linux-password-hashes/) — 2026-08-06
